GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/issues/142

=== CONTEXT (P0 regression guard, pairs with antigravity-booster#11) ===
The antigravity-booster projects a SINGLE-ticket .adlc/tickets.json into each build worktree. When that ticket has an outgoing edge, plugins/adlc-antigravity/core-inline.mjs loadTickets (~lines 51-55) reports 'edge to unknown ticket <id>'; rails-checker.mjs railPreconditions (~lines 222-224) treats any validation error as tamper and fails closed ({state:deny}); checkRail/decide (~line 249, hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs ~line 117) then deny EVERY mutating tool call for the whole session — not just rail paths. The plugin's decide.test.mjs always writes a full ticket set, so the single-ticket projection shape was never tested. The booster-side fix (issue #11) strips edges from the projection; this ticket locks the contract from the plugin side.

=== TASK ===
1. Add tests in plugins/adlc-antigravity/test/ over the projection shapes: (a) single-ticket tickets.json, NO edges, with rails -> hook enforces the rail (denies a rail write) AND allows an in-scope non-rail write; (b) single-ticket tickets.json WITH a dangling edge -> assert the CURRENT fail-closed deny-all behavior explicitly, with a comment linking booster#11 and adlc#142 so the failure mode is visible and intentional in the suite.
2. Document the contract decision (plugin stays fail-closed on dangling edges; booster must project edge-free single-ticket files) in docs/integrations/antigravity.md.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: Both projection-shape tests exist and pass under node --test in plugins/adlc-antigravity/. VERIFY: run the plugin test suite, exit 0, and the two new test names appear in output.
- AC2: The dangling-edge deny-all behavior is asserted (not implicit) with the cross-repo comment. VERIFY: grep the test file for issues/142 and issues/11 references.
- AC3: The contract decision is documented in docs/integrations/antigravity.md. VERIFY: grep for a 'single-ticket projection' section.
- AC4: No production code changes in this ticket — tests + docs only. VERIFY: git diff touches only test/ and docs/.

GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/issues/143

=== CONTEXT (P0, enables booster handshake; pairs with antigravity-booster#12) ===
The plugin carries two conflicting versions: plugins/adlc-antigravity/plugin.json says 0.2.0, plugins/adlc-antigravity/package.json says 1.2.0. Consumers (antigravity-booster) have no way to detect schema/payload drift: today the booster only substring-matches agy plugin list output. Booster issue #12 adds a manifest-based handshake that reads an adlcContract field from the installed plugin.json (installed location: ~/.gemini/config/plugins/adlc-antigravity/plugin.json — agy copies the whole plugin dir).

=== TASK ===
1. Reconcile to ONE version with plugin.json authoritative; make package.json mirror it. Pick the reconciled number deliberately (recommend 1.2.0 since package.json history is the real release lineage) and state the choice in the commit message.
2. Add "adlcContract": 1 to plugin.json, versioning the interfaces: (a) the tickets.json schema accepted by core-inline.mjs, (b) the hook stdin payload shape, (c) the hook decision output shape. Document bump rules (any breaking change to those three interfaces bumps the integer) in a comment-adjacent doc — plugins/adlc-antigravity/README.md (create it — do NOT touch docs/integrations/antigravity.md, which is in ticket A142's scope).
3. Add a test asserting plugin.json and package.json versions agree and adlcContract is a positive integer, so CI fails on future divergence.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: plugin.json and package.json carry the same version; test enforces it. VERIFY: plugin test suite exit 0; intentionally desync locally -> test fails.
- AC2: adlcContract present in plugin.json with documented bump rules. VERIFY: grep plugin.json for adlcContract; grep docs for the bump rules.
- AC3: agy plugin validate plugins/adlc-antigravity still passes (manifest remains agy-loadable). VERIFY: run it, exit 0.
- AC4: Booster issue #12 unblocked: the field is readable from the plugin source dir (no build step required).

tickets.body:
## Problem

`.adlc/current-ticket.json` is the trust root every harness reads to decide which ticket is in flight. Its schema is documented nowhere, and ten hand-copied resolvers read it with two different key sets and three different hash-strictness levels:

| resolver | id keys accepted | ticketHash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| packages/tickets/lib/provenance.mjs (canonical) | id, ticket | required |
| packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs:545 (rails) | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs:1156 (build-gate) | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-cursor/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-antigravity/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs:313 | id, ticket, ticketId | checked if present |
| plugins/adlc-pi/lib/rails-checker.mjs:64 | id, ticket, ticketId | never checked |

TEN resolvers (the tenth, plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-lifecycle.mjs, is advisory narration and was only found at P4 by the boundary test below), three strictness levels, two key sets. SEVEN do not accept `ticketId`.

Live consequence in THIS repo: the pointer is `{"ticketId":"T46","ticketHash":"fc7afc5a..."}`. Seven of the object-pointer resolvers -- including the canonical one -- resolve `id: null` => "no active ticket" => build-gate and the Claude Code rail hook FAIL OPEN and enforce nothing, while codex and pi enforce T46. Verified: `node -e "import('./packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.resolveActiveTicketId({dir:'.',env:{}})))"` prints `{id:null,conflict:false}`.

An object pointer whose id key is unrecognized (misspelled, or a legacy alias a given reader does not know) is silently read as "no pointer at all" => allow. That is a fail-open hole in a trust root. An UNPARSEABLE pointer correctly denies; an UNRECOGNIZED-SCHEMA pointer allows. No code writes the `ticketId` key -- it is hand-authored drift copied from the manifest's evidence field name, which is exactly what an undocumented schema produces.

Contributing causes:
- No documented pointer schema and no JSON schema file.
- The spec-14 generator (scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs) already exists and generates the ticket LOADER into three harnesses, but the RESOLVER was hand-ported into ten copies carrying "KEEP IN SYNC" comments instead.
- doctorTicketStore (packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs:22) reports `{name:'current-ticket', ok:true, present}` unconditionally -- it never parses, resolves, or hash-checks. This repo's stale pointer (T46 is merged work) passes doctor clean. Spec AC11 claims "current-ticket ... checks".
- The only programmatic writer (plugins/adlc-pi/lib/commands.mjs:226) does a bare non-atomic writeFileSync; every hook re-reads the file per tool call, so a torn read is reachable.
- ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT says only "conflicts with current-ticket.json" and never names the actual model: the active ticket is per-worktree state, and parallel work needs a separate worktree (spec 2 and 10.1).

## Build

1. **One canonical resolver.** Move the pointer contract into a new `packages/tickets/lib/pointer.mjs` (parse, validate, resolve, atomic write); `provenance.mjs` delegates to it. Port it into `scripts/ticket-readers/read-only-loader.mjs` and extend `scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs`'s output list to every harness that hand-copies a resolver (codex, claude-code, antigravity, opencode, cursor, pi). Delete the hand copies and their KEEP IN SYNC comments. `packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs` re-exports the canonical resolution rather than reimplementing it.

2. **One key contract, fail-closed on drift.** Canonical `{"id": string, "ticketHash": string}` (spec 11). `ticket` and `ticketId` stay accepted DEPRECATED aliases in EVERY reader so no existing pointer bricks. An object pointer with no recognized id key is INVALID_CURRENT_TICKET => fail closed. This closes the fail-open hole. Deactivation is deleting the file, not writing `{}`. A bare string pointer stays a legacy form behind allowLegacyPointer.

3. **One hash strictness.** Every reader verifies `ticketHash` against `snapshot.ticketHashes[id]` and fails closed on mismatch (ACTIVE_TICKET_STALE). A missing hash is ACTIVE_TICKET_HASH_MISSING => fail closed under the strict default; only the documented 1.x bridge (allowLegacyPointer) downgrades it to a warning. No reader may silently skip a hash that is present.

4. **Doctor validates.** doctorTicketStore parses the pointer, resolves the id against the snapshot, verifies the hash, and reports ok:false plus the stable code for unparseable, unrecognized schema, absent ticket, missing hash, and stale hash; ok:true with a deprecation warning for an alias pointer. --json carries {present, id, code, deprecatedAlias}.

5. **Atomic writes.** Add `writeActiveTicket(root, ticket)` to pointer.mjs: write a temp file in the same directory then renameSync into place, always emitting `{id, ticketHash}`. plugins/adlc-pi/lib/commands.mjs uses it. A concurrent reader observes the old or the new pointer, never a partial one.

6. **Name the model in the error.** ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT states that the active ticket is per-worktree state and that parallel work on a second ticket needs its own worktree (`git worktree add`), not a second pointer.

7. **Document it.** Add packages/tickets/schemas/current-ticket.schema.json; document the schema, the worktree rule, and the alias deprecation in every docs/integrations/*.md that mentions the pointer, and record the deprecation in the 1.x-to-2.0 timeline in docs/specs/sharded-ticket-store.md.

8. **Repair this repo's live pointer** to the canonical form, or delete it since T46 is merged work (doctor will now report it).

## Decision record: hash strictness during 1.x (settled, do not re-litigate)

Repo evidence, gathered at P2:
- `packages/tickets/test/provenance.test.mjs:14` writes `{id, ticketHash}` -- the domain package is STRICT.
- `plugins/adlc-cursor/test/{rails-guard,pretool-dispatch}.test.mjs:28`, `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/review.test.mjs:47` all write `{id: currentTicket}` -- HASH-LESS. The harness layer's de facto contract omits the hash.
- Every `docs/integrations/*.md` offers the pointer as an option ("Active ticket via `ADLC_TICKET` or `.adlc/current-ticket.json`") and NEVER shows its schema, so a hand-written hash-less `{"id":"T1"}` is the expected state in the wild.

Therefore making harness readers strict-by-default would fail the existing harness suites AND deny every real install that took the documented file route -- punishing users for our own missing documentation. The decision:

- **The fail-OPEN hole is fixed unconditionally and immediately** (an object pointer with no recognized id key denies). This is the actual security defect and it is not bridged.
- **A missing `ticketHash` is bridged through 1.x**: harness readers default `allowLegacyPointer: true` and emit a deprecation warning; `@adlc/tickets`' own API keeps `allowLegacyPointer: false` (strict) as its default. A missing hash loses only stale-detection -- rails still enforce against the current ticket -- so it is a weaker guarantee, not a hole.
- **A PRESENT `ticketHash` is always verified in every reader**, bridge or not. Silently skipping a present hash is never permitted.
- **2.0 removes the bridge** (recorded in the spec-13 timeline by Build step 7).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 -- one implementation.** No hand-copied resolver remains; every harness resolver is the generated file or an import of it. A grep for 'KEEP IN SYNC' is NOT an acceptable verifier -- those comments were present and still wrong, and the grep false-positives on the pointer's legitimate appearances (a rail glob) and on ordinary \`ticket.id ?? '?'\` handling. The verifier is a boundary test that proves nobody parses the pointer themselves, and that fails on a planted hand-rolled reader. Verify: `node scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs --check` exits 0 AND `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs` exits 0 AND `node --test scripts/test/ticket-store-boundary.test.mjs` exits 0.
- **AC2 -- reader agreement, no fail-open.** A table-driven test runs every reader (canonical, generated, build-gate, and each harness) over a shared vector set and asserts identical decisions: `{"tickett":"T46"}` denies with INVALID_CURRENT_TICKET in all; `{"ticketId":"T46",...}` and `{"id":"T46",...}` resolve T46 in all. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='reader agreement'` exits 0.
- **AC3 -- live-bug regression.** The exact live pointer `{"ticketId":"T46","ticketHash":"fc7afc5a0a6517d908988afa6cd6eeb1a5fa918a8b91fd548f910798ef50191d"}` resolves to T46 in every reader, and no reader returns a no-active-ticket allow for an object pointer that carries any id-like key. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='live pointer regression'` exits 0.
- **AC4 -- hash strictness unified.** A PRESENT ticketHash that does not match the snapshot denies with ACTIVE_TICKET_STALE in every reader THAT HOLDS A SNAPSHOT. Boundary found at P4: @adlc/build-gate.resolveActiveTicketId({dir, env}) resolves IDENTITY and takes no snapshot (its bin loads the store separately), so staleness/absence/hash-missing are decidable only where the store is loaded; build-gate must still resolve the id and never report "no active ticket" for those vectors, which the rail asserts explicitly. A MISSING hash denies under the strict default (`@adlc/tickets`) and warns-but-resolves under the 1.x bridge default used by harness readers. Existing harness tests that write hash-less `{id}` pointers keep passing unchanged. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='hash'` exits 0.
- **AC5 -- doctor validates.** Doctor returns ok:false plus the stable code for unparseable, unrecognized-schema, absent-ticket, missing-hash, and stale-hash pointers; ok:true with deprecatedAlias:true for an alias pointer; ok:true for a canonical one. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='current-ticket'` exits 0.
- **AC6 -- atomic write.** writeActiveTicket renames into place from a same-directory temp file, and a test asserting no partial pointer is observable passes. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='atomic'` exits 0.
- **AC7 -- error names the model.** The ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT message contains "worktree". Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='conflict message'` exits 0.
- **AC8 -- no harness regression.** Verify: `node scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs --check && node scripts/codex-install-smoke.mjs . && node scripts/cursor-install-smoke.mjs . && node scripts/antigravity-install-smoke.mjs .` exits 0.
- **AC9 -- suite green.** Verify: `npm test` exits 0.
- **AC10 -- documented.** packages/tickets/schemas/current-ticket.schema.json exists and admits the canonical and alias forms while rejecting an unrecognized-key object; every docs/integrations/*.md that mentions the pointer shows the schema and the worktree rule. Verify: `node --test scripts/test/ticket-store-docs.test.mjs` exits 0.
tickets.title: Make .adlc/current-ticket.json one validated, fail-closed, generated contract across every resolver

tickets.body:
## Problem

The release pipeline has a fail-closed drift gate (`findVersionDrift`, scripts/release.mjs:144) whose stated purpose is to make "the v1.1.0 drift can't happen again" machine-checkable. It validates the **source tree**. Nothing validates the **artifact a user actually installs**. Two live defects follow from that one gap.

### Defect A — Claude Code plugin stranded at 0.2.0 across every release since 1.2.x

`scripts/release.mjs` grew host-specific bump loops as integrations were added: `codexPluginManifestPaths` (line 112), `cursorPluginManifestPaths` (line 122), `cursorMarketplacePath` (line 132). Claude Code was the FIRST integration and never got one. Neither did antigravity's flat `plugin.json`.

Observed state at 1.5.0:

| manifest | bumped by release.mjs | version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| packages/*/package.json | yes | 1.5.0 |
| plugins/*/package.json | yes | 1.5.0 |
| plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json | yes | 1.5.0 |
| plugins/*/.cursor-plugin/plugin.json | yes | 1.5.0 |
| .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json | yes | 1.5.0 |
| **.claude-plugin/marketplace.json** | **NO** | **0.2.0** |
| **plugins/adlc-claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json** | **NO** | **0.2.0** |
| **plugins/adlc-antigravity/plugin.json** | **NO** | **0.2.0** (its package.json is 1.5.0) |

`findVersionDrift` mirrors the exact same blind spots — it reads codex manifests (line 150), cursor manifests (line 154), and the cursor marketplace (line 158), and never opens anything under `.claude-plugin/`. So 1.3.0, 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 all passed a GREEN drift gate while Claude Code sat at 0.2.0.

Why Cursor never drifted and Claude Code did — the smoke tests are asymmetric:
- `scripts/cursor-install-smoke.mjs:145-157` asserts marketplace `entry.version`, marketplace `metadata.version`, AND `plugin.json` version are each in lockstep with the package version.
- `scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs:103` asserts only `if (!plugin.version) fail(...)` — pure truthiness, compared against nothing. `0.2.0` satisfies it forever.

Root design gap: `plugins/adlc-claude-code/` ships NO package.json, so there was no per-package version to lockstep against, and the cursor pattern was never copied. The lockstep target must therefore be the root package.json version.

User-visible harm: the Claude Code marketplace is git-sourced off the default branch, so pushing main IS publishing — but `/plugin` compares the declared `version` string to decide whether an update exists. Because that string never moved, every release since 1.2.x was invisible to the updater. `/plugin` reports "adlc is already at the latest version (0.2.0)" while main carries 1.5.0 content. Reproduced live 2026-07-20.

### Defect B — @adlc/ticket-sync ships a tarball missing a file its own code imports

`packages/ticket-sync/package.json` declares `files: [bin/, lib/, schemas/, README.md, LICENSE]`. `packages/ticket-sync/lib/doctor.mjs:13` has a TOP-LEVEL `import { generateAll } from '../scripts/gen-schema.mjs'`. `scripts/` is not in the allowlist, so the file is not published.

Verified against the real published artifact, not inferred:

    npm pack @adlc/ticket-sync@1.5.0 && tar tzf adlc-ticket-sync-1.5.0.tgz | grep -E 'scripts|doctor'
    => package/lib/doctor.mjs        (present)
    => (no scripts/gen-schema.mjs)   (absent)

Consequence: `adlc ticket doctor` hard-crashes with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for EVERY npm-installed user of @adlc/cli@1.5.0. Reproduced live 2026-07-20 against the globally installed CLI.

A survey of all 29 packages/* shows ticket-sync is the ONLY package whose shipped code reaches outside its `files` allowlist (every other package's relative imports stay within `../lib/`). So the defect is isolated — but it is live and it breaks a documented command.

### Shared root cause

Both defects are invisible to `npm test` because every test runs against the source tree, where the files exist and the versions are irrelevant. No gate ever asks "does the thing we are about to publish actually work when installed?"

## Build

1. **Generalize the bump, do not add a third hardcoded pair.** Replace `codexPluginManifestPaths`/`cursorPluginManifestPaths` with one glob-driven discovery in scripts/release.mjs covering `plugins/*/.*-plugin/plugin.json` (codex, cursor, claude-code, and any future host for free) and `plugins/*/plugin.json` (antigravity's flat layout). Replace `cursorMarketplacePath` with discovery of every root `.*-plugin/marketplace.json`, bumping `metadata.version` and every `plugins[].version`. Adding a new host directory must be drift-protected on day one, not the release after someone notices.

2. **Close the same blind spots in `findVersionDrift`.** It must use the identical discovery functions as the bump, so the gate cannot structurally diverge from the bumper again. A manifest the bumper touches but the gate does not check is the exact shape of this bug.

3. **Add artifact-completeness verification.** For every non-private publish target, resolve the static import graph reachable from its `bin/` and `lib/` entrypoints and assert every resolved relative specifier falls inside a path admitted by that package's `files` allowlist. Fail closed at bump time, before any tag or publish, in the same place the existing provenance/metadata gate lives (scripts/release.mjs:302).

4. **Fix Defect B.** Either add `scripts/` to @adlc/ticket-sync's `files`, or move `gen-schema.mjs` into `lib/`. Prefer moving it into `lib/` — `scripts/` reads as build tooling and shipping it invites the same confusion later. Whichever is chosen, step 3's gate must fail on the pre-fix state.

5. **Fix Defect A's stranded values.** Bring `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (metadata + entry), `plugins/adlc-claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and `plugins/adlc-antigravity/plugin.json` to the current version via the generalized bumper — not by hand-editing, so the fix proves the mechanism.

6. **Harden the Claude Code smoke test to match Cursor's.** `scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs:103` must lockstep plugin.json version, marketplace `metadata.version`, and marketplace `entry.version` against the ROOT package.json version (adlc-claude-code has no package.json of its own). Preserve the existing `additionalProperties:false` key guard at lines 118-129 — CC rejects unknown plugin.json fields, so the allowlist must not gain a field as a side effect.

7. **Record the decision.** ADR documenting that release gates validate the published artifact, not the source tree, and that host-manifest discovery is glob-driven by design.

## Out of scope

- Migrating the legacy `.adlc/tickets.json` store to sharded tickets.
- Any change to the publish ORDER or provenance/OIDC mechanism (working correctly).
- Adding a package.json to plugins/adlc-claude-code — the root version is the lockstep target instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — claude-plugin manifests bump.** After `releaseMain('9.9.9')` runs against a fixture containing `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugins/adlc-claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, both are at 9.9.9 including marketplace `metadata.version` and every `plugins[].version`. VERIFY: `node --test scripts/test/release-artifact.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='claude-plugin bump'` exits 0.

- **AC2 — drift gate catches the stranded state, and fails on the pre-fix code.** `findVersionDrift('9.9.9', fixture)` returns a non-empty list naming `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` metadata.version, its plugin entry, `plugins/adlc-claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and a flat `plugins/*/plugin.json` when each is stranded at 0.2.0. This test must FAIL against the current implementation — a test that passes before the fix proves nothing. VERIFY: `node --test scripts/test/release-artifact.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='drift'` exits 0 after the fix, and `git stash`-ing scripts/release.mjs makes it exit non-zero.

- **AC3 — discovery is glob-driven, not enumerated.** A fixture containing an invented host directory (`plugins/adlc-future/.future-plugin/plugin.json` and root `.future-plugin/marketplace.json`) at a stale version is both bumped and drift-flagged with NO change to release.mjs. This is the criterion that distinguishes the real fix from a third hardcoded pair. VERIFY: `node --test scripts/test/release-artifact.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='unknown host'` exits 0.

- **AC4 — artifact completeness catches Defect B.** The new gate, run against a fixture package whose lib/ imports `../scripts/x.mjs` while `files` omits `scripts/`, reports that package as a problem; run against the same fixture with `scripts/` admitted, it reports nothing. VERIFY: `node --test scripts/test/release-artifact.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='files allowlist'` exits 0.

- **AC5 — Defect B is actually fixed in the real repo.** `adlc ticket doctor` runs to completion against a real install built from this tree (no ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND), and the artifact-completeness gate reports zero problems across all packages/*. VERIFY: `npm pack` @adlc/ticket-sync from the working tree, extract to a temp dir, and `node -e "import('<tmp>/lib/doctor.mjs')"` resolves; asserted by `node --test scripts/test/release-artifact.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='ticket-sync doctor'`.

- **AC6 — Claude Code smoke locksteps like Cursor's.** `scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs` fails when plugin.json version, marketplace metadata.version, or marketplace entry.version diverges from the root package.json version, and the `additionalProperties:false` allowlist guard still rejects an extra plugin.json field. VERIFY: `node --test scripts/test/claude-code-plugin-smoke.test.mjs` exits 0 and includes a case for each of the three divergences plus the extra-field guard.

- **AC7 — the real repo is in lockstep.** `findVersionDrift` against the actual working tree at the current root version returns an empty list, and `node scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs .` exits 0. VERIFY: both commands run against the repo exit 0.

- **AC8 — no regression.** VERIFY: `npm test` exits 0.

- **AC9 — decision recorded.** An ADR under docs/adr/ states that release gates validate the published artifact and that host-manifest discovery is glob-driven. VERIFY: the ADR file exists and is referenced from scripts/release.mjs's header comment.

## P1 premortem findings (fold into Build; verified with evidence 2026-07-20)

- **F1 — recursive globbing would corrupt 21 worktree copies (HIGH).** `find . -name marketplace.json -path '*plugin*'` returns 21 hits under `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/`. Discovery MUST be depth-EXACT — root `<root>/.<host>-plugin/marketplace.json` and `<pluginsDir>/<name>/.<host>-plugin/plugin.json` only, resolved from the injected root/pluginsDir params. No `**` recursion, no walking into `.worktrees`, `.claude`, or `node_modules`. Build step 1 and 2 are amended accordingly, and AC3's fixture must include a decoy at `.worktrees/x/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` that the gate must NOT flag.

- **F2 — do not reimplement npm files semantics; ask npm (HIGH).** `npm pack --dry-run --json` returns the authoritative shipped-file list (verified: 24 files for @adlc/ticket-sync, `lib/doctor.mjs` present, no `scripts/` entry). Build step 3 is amended: resolve each package's relative import graph, then check membership against `npm pack --dry-run --json` output rather than prefix-matching the `files` array. This avoids reimplementing files/.npmignore/always-included interplay, and it re-confirms Defect B from the WORKING TREE rather than only the published tarball.

- **F3 — check relative specifiers only.** The import scan must ignore `node:` builtins and bare package specifiers (`@adlc/core`), which are dependency-resolved not file-shipped. It must cover static `import`/`export ... from`; a dynamic `import()` with a computed specifier is undecidable and is explicitly out of scope — note that limitation in the gate's output rather than pretending coverage.

- **F4 — never create manifests, only update existing ones.** `scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs` lines 58-87 assert the NESTED `plugins/adlc-claude-code/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` does NOT exist (a dual-resolution failure on live install). The generalized bumper must only rewrite files that already exist.

- **F5 — antigravity's plugin.json carries `adlcContract: 1`.** Bump `version` only; `adlcContract` is a protocol number, not a release version, and must be left untouched. AC1 must assert this.

- **F6 — release sequencing.** Bringing the stranded manifests to 1.5.0 is honest (main carries 1.5.0 content), but users cached at 0.2.0 only re-pull on a version CHANGE. Build the FIRST shippable increment of the OpenCode integration: the in-process rails-guard plugin plus the discovery skill, implementing the unbuilt core of the existing design. This ticket was reconciled (2026-06-27) against substantial prior work on branch `opencode-integration` — DO NOT re-derive the design or rebuild what already exists.

=== AUTHORITATIVE DESIGN (the contract — read first) ===
The full OpenCode integration is already designed on branch `opencode-integration` (NOT yet merged to main):
- docs/opencode-integration-plan.md — the 6-phase (A-F) delivery plan and the in-process hook contract. THIS is the design contract; do not contradict it.
- docs/opencode.md — the adoption guide.
Read both via `git show opencode-integration:docs/opencode-integration-plan.md` and `git show opencode-integration:docs/opencode.md`. Treat their primitive mapping (§3), directory structure (§4.1), hook contract (§4.2), and phased plan (§7) as the spec.

=== WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — DO NOT REBUILD (reconciliation) ===
1. Phase F CI backstop is IMPLEMENTED on `opencode-integration`: docs/ci/rails-guard.yml (hardened: codeowners attestation, signed runner pool, trust-root freeze, monotonic config invariants), scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs (+295), and ~1800 lines of tests (scripts/test/rails-guard-bootstrap-ci.test.mjs, scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs). The unbypassable second enforcement layer therefore ALREADY EXISTS. Do not re-author it. The ONLY deferred CI item relevant here (plan §6.2) is protecting `.opencode/plugin/` and `.opencode/opencode.json` paths — note it as Phase F follow-up; do not implement it in this ticket.
2. @adlc/core (v1.1.0) is published and is the single source of truth for rails logic (plan §6.6). The plugin MUST delegate to it, NOT inline-port the adlc-pi helpers (the duplicated legacy CC/codex hooks are explicitly flagged as tech debt to remove).

=== RESOLVED OpenCode plugin API (P1 research + plan, pin in ADR 0004) ===
- Package: @opencode-ai/plugin v1.17.11 (peerDependency). Backend is Bun/JS in-process (plan §2).
- Discovery/load: the SHIPPED source lives in this repo at plugins/adlc-opencode/ (mirroring plugins/adlc-codex, plugins/adlc-pi); /adlc-init copies/symlinks it into the user's .opencode/plugin/adlc-opencode/ and registers it in .opencode/opencode.json (plan §4.1, Phase A). OpenCode loads the pre-bundled dist/index.js.
- Edit-interception hook: "tool.execute.before", async (input, output) => {...}. VERIFY-FIRST and pin in ADR 0004: (i) whether the edited path is input.args.filePath or output.args.filePath (docs vs gist conflict) — capture a real edit AND write payload; (ii) the full set of file-mutating tool names in v1.17.11 (edit/write/patch/multiedit/apply_patch).
- CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT-CAPABILITY GATE (plan §Phase D — resolves the earlier 'does throw abort the write?' question): the in-session hook MUST NOT be labelled/treated as enforcing unless the installed OpenCode SDK supports `onFailure: deny` AND a runtime capability probe confirms it. If unsupported, the hook is ADVISORY only and preflight FAILS CLOSED unless `allowAdvisoryHooks: true` is explicitly configured. The unbypassable layer remains the CI gate (already built).
- Workspace root: PIN which plugin context field (project/directory/worktree) is the repo root for locating .adlc/.

=== RAIL CONTRACT — delegate to @adlc/core, preserve sibling semantics ===
The thin adapter (rails-checker.ts) maps OpenCode hook args to @adlc/core and must preserve the contract both sibling hooks implement (plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs, plugins/adlc-pi/index.ts):
1. Active ticket via process.env.ADLC_TICKET OR .adlc/current-ticket.json; conflict => fail closed.
2. Enforce only when process.env.ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT === '1'; else no-op.
3. Rails = the SINGLE active ticket's rails PLUS implicit trust-root rails '.adlc/tickets.json' and '.adlc/current-ticket.json'. NOT a union across tickets.
4. No-op fail-safe when .adlc/tickets.json absent, enforcement off, no active ticket, or empty declared rails (trust-root still frozen).
5. On a rail match, deny via the SDK's onFailure:deny contract (per the capability gate above), naming the rail + ticket.

=== DELIVERABLES (this MVP increment only) ===
1. plugins/adlc-opencode/ — Node package mirroring the sibling integrations: package.json (@adlc/opencode-package, type module, peerDependency @opencode-ai/plugin >=1.17.11, dependency @adlc/core), index.ts (the Plugin named export wiring tool.execute.before), rails-checker.ts (thin adapter importing @adlc/core rails logic — NO inlined re-implementation), a pre-bundled dist/index.js, and skill/adlc.md (the phase-routing discovery skill, copied/adapted from the sibling skill sentinels IF OpenCode's skill format matches; verify first).
2. scripts/opencode-install-smoke.mjs — mirrors scripts/codex-install-smoke.mjs / scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs: validate the plugin package shape, the dist bundle, the hook wiring, skill registration, and that the deny path delegates to @adlc/core. Must not require the opencode binary and must not mutate the user environment.
3. docs/integrations/opencode.md — replace the 'no integration exists yet' stub with a real landing doc that LINKS the authoritative plan (docs/opencode-integration-plan.md) and docs/opencode.md, documents this MVP increment + the two-layer enforcement (advisory in-session hook gated on onFailure:deny + the already-built mandatory CI gate), Install (local verification via the smoke test), the Formal ADLC Coverage table, and Gaps (the unbuilt Phases A/B/C/E below; the deferred .opencode/plugin path protection).
4. docs/adr/0004-adlc-opencode-integration.md — formal ADR pointing to the plan as the detailed design, pinning the resolved API facts (i)-(ii), the onFailure:deny capability gate, and a Threat Model section (the in-session bypass surface; CI gate as mitigation).

OUT OF SCOPE (now authored as follow-on tickets T2 Phase A / T3 Phase B / T4 Phase C / T5 Phase E — note them in the ADR Gaps, do not build here): the full slash-command suite (/adlc-ticket../adlc-maintain), the keyless two-phase LLM bridge, the advisory session hooks, the 5-lens prosecutor subagents + verifier, and the .opencode/plugin path-protection CI follow-up.

VERIFY: test exercises each via the real handler and exits 0.
- AC4: docs/integrations/opencode.md no longer contains 'no integration exists yet', links docs/opencode-integration-plan.md, and has Install + Formal ADLC Coverage table + Gaps. VERIFY: grep for absence of the banner, presence of the plan link, and the three headings.

tickets.body:
Two cross-model (codex/GPT) adversarial-review findings on the merged T9 push/create path (PR #33). FIX both with TDD.

Finding 1 (HIGH, duplicate issues under the DEFAULT label-scoped selector): createIssue attaches no label, and the create adoption scan only searches the selector-scoped issue list and ignores the nodeId/number already stored in pendingCreates. A crash after the remote create but before renderAndPush labels the issue leaves an UNLABELED orphan that the next run's label-scoped listIssues cannot see, so adoption misses and a DUPLICATE issue is created. Fix: (a) when pendingCreates[key] carries a number/nodeId, adopt that issue DIRECTLY (verify via issue view) instead of relying on the selector-scoped body scan; (b) attach the configured createLabel at create time so the new issue immediately belongs to the selected set. The body-key scan remains the fallback when pendingCreates was lost.

Finding 2 (HIGH, stale edges published to the tracker): the create loop reads `desired = pickBlock(t)` from the ORIGINAL localTickets snapshot, but reassignId rewrites the working `tickets` array. A dependent ticket created later (T8 edges->T7) serializes its STALE T<n> edge into the remote issue body + syncedHash while tickets.json gets the rewritten gh: edge, leaving the tracker an invalid sync source until the next push. Fix: in the create loop, derive `desired` from the CURRENT reassigned working `tickets` entry (by id), not the stale snapshot.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/github.test.mjs: the stateful fake's listIssues HONORS the label selector (only returns issues carrying the selected labels). A new test: create succeeds, labeling is skipped/crashes (unlabeled orphan) -> a re-run with a label-scoped selector ADOPTS via pendingCreates (no second `issue create` call); assert exactly one remote issue.
2. test/github.test.mjs: createIssue attaches the configured createLabel at create time (the new issue is in the label-scoped selection immediately).
3. test/github.test.mjs: multi-create T7 + T8(edges->T7) under --write -> assert T8's REMOTE issue body block carries edge to gh:owner/repo#<T7-number>, NOT 'T7'; and its sidecar syncedHash matches the rewritten block.
4. Full suite green; re-prosecute with adlc:prosecutor (P5) to CLEAR; THEN a cross-model adversarial-review pass (codex) before merge (the lesson from this finding).

Events pinned against docs: preToolUse (blockable, JSON stdin/stdout, permission allow|deny|ask), afterFileEdit (observational, cannot block), beforeShellExecution, beforeReadFile. Deny a structured edit when the active ticket is high-risk AND the session context-fitness signal is degraded, unless ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 with an audited gate-manifest record. 2. flail (afterFileEdit, piggyback in adlc-audit.mjs): after the rail audit, run the flail heuristics (packages/flail-detector primitives) over the hook's own persisted recent-edits window; advisory stderr notice only.

Phase 1a of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md (committed on this branch — READ IT FIRST; it is the contract). Fixes the correctness core of plugins/adlc-pi and completes the ADR-0004 core-delegation work that was done for cursor/opencode (#97/#102) but skipped for pi.

=== VERIFIED pi API FACTS (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent v0.80.3) ===
- pi loads extensions as TypeScript via jiti; there is NO compile step. The checked-in plugins/adlc-pi/index.js is a hand-compiled artifact and must be deleted.
- CRITICAL BUG: the `before_agent_start` result `{systemPrompt}` REPLACES the turn's system prompt (chained across extensions); the documented pattern is `event.systemPrompt + "..."` (see BeforeAgentStartEventResult in the package's dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts and docs/extensions.md, which shows `systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + "\n\nExtra instructions..."`). Current index.ts returns ONLY the ADLC doctrine block — wiping pi's entire built-in system prompt whenever a ticket is active — and only an error banner on config load errors.
- `tool_call` events are a per-tool discriminated union (narrow with `isToolCallEventType`); `event.input` is mutable; returning `{block:true, reason}` blocks the call. tool_call also fires for custom third-party tools.
- pi packaging rules: the pi core packages (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, @earendil-works/pi-ai, pi-agent-core, pi-tui, typebox) must remain peerDependencies and must never be bundled; regular npm deps like @adlc/core go in dependencies.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Append-not-replace: both the ticket-doctrine path AND the load-error path of before_agent_start return `{systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + BLOCK}`.
2. Restructure to sibling architecture (mirror plugins/adlc-opencode): thin index.ts event wiring; all logic in plugins/adlc-pi/lib/*.mjs, including a rails-checker.mjs THIN adapter delegating every primitive to @adlc/core (globMatch, loadTickets, validateTicket, inScope, path canonicalization, and the classifyShellCommand / collectShellPaths / shellHasMutation family). Delete the hand-rolled implementations. node --test tests target the lib .mjs files directly. Delete plugins/adlc-pi/index.js from the tree. package.json `pi.extensions` keeps pointing at ./index.ts.
3. Shell enforcement ladder (codex/opencode parity, replacing the naive regexes): parseable mutating command touching a rail or out-of-scope path → deny; opaque mutation (e.g. `curl … | sh`) → deny with explanation (fail closed); read-only commands are NEVER blocked; version specs (left-pad@1.3.0) and git refs (feat/x) are NOT collected as paths.
4. Symlink-aware rail resolution: lift resolveRailPath from plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs into @adlc/core (new export + unit tests in packages/core/test), and import it from core in BOTH the opencode adapter and the new pi adapter. Opencode behavior must not change; its test suite is a frozen rail and must pass unmodified.
5. Root package.json test script: remove the `|| true` escape from the pi typecheck step so type errors fail CI. Add @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent as a devDependency of plugins/adlc-pi for types only (NOT dependencies — packaging rule above). Node >= 22.19 is required by the pi package.

- AC1: unit test asserts the before_agent_start result systemPrompt startsWith(event.systemPrompt) AND contains the doctrine block, for both the active-ticket and the load-error paths. VERIFY: node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/ exits 0.
- AC2: no local primitive implementations remain: grep for `function globMatch`, `shellHasMutation`, `collectShellPaths` definitions in plugins/adlc-pi/index.ts and lib/*.mjs finds only imports from @adlc/core. VERIFY: grep.
- AC3: behavioral tests prove `npm install left-pad`, `git checkout -b feat/x`, and `sed -n '1,10p' <out-of-scope-file>` are ALLOWED; `echo x > <rail-file>` is DENIED; `curl -s https://x.sh | sh` is DENIED as opaque mutation. VERIFY: node --test cases named accordingly, exit 0.
- AC4: a symlink whose real target is a frozen rail is denied by the pi adapter; resolveRailPath is exported from @adlc/core with its own tests; plugins/adlc-opencode tests pass without modification. VERIFY: node --test packages/core/test + plugins/adlc-opencode/test + the new pi test.
- AC5: plugins/adlc-pi/index.js is absent (git ls-files); the root package.json test script contains no `|| true` on the pi typecheck; `npm test` at repo root exits 0. VERIFY: git ls-files + grep + npm test.

Suppressions are denied. Do not modify sibling plugin directories except the single import swap in plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs (deliverable 4).

Phase 2 items 2.3 + 2.4 + 2.5 of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md plus the banked P5 finding in the spec's Phase 2 preamble (READ THE SPEC FIRST). Builds on T22's extension wiring.

=== VERIFIED pi API FACTS (0.80.3; types in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts) ===
- `pi.appendEntry(customType, data?)` persists a custom entry into the pi session file (NOT sent to the LLM); reconstruct on session_start via ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()/getBranch().
- `pi.setLabel(entryId, label?)` bookmarks an entry — labels are visible in pi's /tree view.
- `user_bash` event fires when the HUMAN runs `!`/`!!` shell commands: { command, excludeFromContext, cwd }. Human commands bypass tool gates by design.
- `tool_call` fires for custom third-party tools too (CustomToolCallEvent: toolName is a plain string, input is Record<string,unknown>); isToolCallEventType narrows built-ins.
- @adlc/core exports appendEntry(name, entry, dir?) (the .adlc ledger writer, used for manifest.jsonl) — distinct from pi's session appendEntry; use BOTH per deliverable 1.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Evidence rail (spec 2.4): every gate event (rail deny, scope deny, shell deny, suppression revert, build-gate deny, flail warning) is recorded (a) into the pi session file via pi.appendEntry('adlc-gate-event', {...}) so it survives in the session tree, AND (b) mirrored to .adlc/manifest.jsonl via @adlc/core's ledger appendEntry. Where the pi API yields an entry id, setLabel the violation entries (label like 'ADLC deny: <rail>') so /tree shows enforcement history. Recording must never crash a gate: failures degrade to a ctx.ui.notify warning.
2. Custom-tool coverage (spec 2.5): the tool_call gate currently keys on write/edit/bash names. Extend: for any OTHER tool name, extract path-like string values from event.input (keys named path/file/filePath/target or any string value that resolves inside the repo); if any resolves to a frozen rail (railHit) → deny. If the tool name is unknown AND the input carries NO extractable path AND the tool is not in a small READONLY allowlist (read/grep/find/ls — see opencode's READONLY_TOOLS precedent) → leave it ungated but record an 'unvetted-tool' evidence entry (pi custom tools legitimately include no-file-target tools; the snapshot/diff reactive gate plus CI remain the backstop — this matches spec 2.5's layered posture, and hard fail-closed for every unknown tool would break pi package ecosystems).
3. user_bash advisory (spec 2.3): on a user_bash event whose command classifies as a mutation touching a frozen rail (reuse checkShellCommand — decision only), do NOT block (human override is legitimate) but notify a warning and record an evidence entry marking a human rail mutation.
4. Position-aware suppression diff (banked P5 finding): diffAddedLines' multiset semantics miss a pre-existing identical marker line RELOCATED from inert to operative position (e.g. moved out of a fenced block). Fix: in scanAddedLines (or a successor), when a file's new content contains a marker on an operative line, flag it if that marker was NOT present on any operative line of the OLD content — i.e. compare operative-marker sets before/after rather than relying only on added-line counts. Keep the existing added-lines path for performance; the operative-set comparison runs only when the quick scan found markers anywhere in the new content.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: a rail deny and a suppression revert each produce (a) a pi session appendEntry call with customType 'adlc-gate-event' and (b) a line in .adlc/manifest.jsonl; a failing ledger write does not prevent the deny itself. VERIFY: node --test with the fake pi capturing appendEntry, plus a real temp-dir manifest assertion.
- AC2: a synthetic third-party tool call {toolName:'write_file', input:{file:'<rail path>'}} is DENIED; the same tool against an in-scope path is not blocked; a no-path unknown tool ('run_linter', input:{}) is allowed AND recorded as 'unvetted-tool'. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC3: a symlink passed through a custom tool's path arg is resolved (railHit's symlink awareness applies) and denied. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC4: user_bash with a rail-mutating command produces a warning notice + evidence entry and does NOT block; a read-only user_bash produces nothing. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC5: a file whose old content had a marker inside a fenced .mdx block and whose new content has the SAME marker line moved outside the fence is FLAGGED, even though the multiset of lines is unchanged; the reverse move (operative → fenced) is NOT flagged. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0; `node scripts/pi-live-deny.mjs` passes.

PROBLEM. The CI rail-freeze gate has no notion of ticket COMPLETION. `scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` builds the frozen-rail set by UNIONing the `rails` arrays of EVERY ticket in the trusted base `.adlc/tickets.json` (see the loop "for (const t of baseTickets) for (const r of t.rails ?? []) rails.push(r)"). It never consults whether a ticket is done. So once a ticket ships, its build-time sibling-freeze rails stay frozen indefinitely, blocking unrelated future work that legitimately touches those paths — until a human performs an admin edit on main (`ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1`, byte-splicing the ticket's `rails` to `[]`).

EVIDENCE (this is not hypothetical). During the opencode T30–T35 continuation the gap forced THREE separate operator-authorized admin rail lifts on main:
- T20/T21 (pi Phase 1) rails lifted after #118 merged (they froze plugins/adlc-opencode/** etc.).
- T22–T25 (pi Phase 2–3) narrowed (dropped plugins/adlc-opencode/**) after #121/#122, then
- T22–T25 rails lifted entirely when a later ticket (T34) needed to edit docs/ci/adlc-maintenance.yml, which they still froze via docs/ci/**.
Each lift is a manual, audited, error-prone byte-splice of the shared trust-root file.

GOAL. A completed ticket's rails should stop contributing to the frozen set automatically, so rails-guard only enforces rails for work that is still IN FLIGHT — without weakening enforcement for active tickets or opening a bypass (a ticket must not be able to mark ITSELF done to unfreeze its own rails mid-build).

DESIGN DIRECTION (the executor picks the concrete mechanism; both are acceptable if they meet the ACs):
Option A — completion-aware union: rails-guard-ci.mjs skips a base ticket's rails when that ticket has trusted completion evidence. "Completed" must be derived from a TRUSTED, HARD-TO-FORGE signal, NOT a self-declared ticket field (a builder could set status:done to unfreeze). Candidates, in order of trust: (a) the ticket's scope files are all present AND the ticket has a manifest `type: p5-complete` / `p6-acceptance-packet` entry in the base `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` (append-only, already CI-protected); (b) the ticket id appears in a merged-work ledger. The union skips a ticket iff its completion evidence is present in the BASE ref (never HEAD — same trust-root discipline the gate already uses for rails).
Option B — lifecycle field on rails that clears at P6: rails move to P3 rail-write time and are cleared when the ticket reaches P6 integrate, recorded in the manifest chain; rails-guard reads only currently-frozen (P3-written, not-yet-P6-cleared) rails.

Whichever: the change is to the ENFORCEMENT gate + its trust model, so it is security-sensitive — it must FAIL CLOSED (a ticket whose completion evidence is absent/ambiguous/unverifiable stays FROZEN), and it must be adversarially reviewed at P1→P2 (can a builder forge completion to unfreeze rails mid-build?).

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification) ===
AC1: A base ticket with TRUSTED completion evidence no longer contributes its rails to the frozen set — a PR that edits a path only that ticket froze PASSES rails-guard. (verify: unit test in scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs — a completed-ticket fixture + a diff touching its rail path → exit 0.)
AC2: An IN-FLIGHT ticket (no completion evidence) still freezes its rails — the same edit is DENIED. (verify: same test file, in-flight fixture → exit 2.)
AC3: FAIL CLOSED on forge/ambiguity — a ticket that self-declares done (e.g. a status field) WITHOUT the trusted evidence stays frozen; unverifiable/partial evidence stays frozen. (verify: test asserts a forged-completion fixture still denies.)
AC4: No self-unfreeze mid-build — completion evidence is read from the BASE ref only (never HEAD), mirroring how rails-guard already reads the rail set, so a builder cannot add completion evidence in their own PR to unfreeze their rails. (verify: test that HEAD-only completion evidence does NOT lift the freeze.)
AC5: The manual admin-lift path is documented as no-longer-routine (docs/ci/rails-guard.yml comment or docs/integrations/*.md), and the recurring-lift history is retired. (verify: read the doc.)
AC6: Full suite green incl. the existing rails-guard-ci tests (verify: npm test exit 0).

NON-GOALS: retroactively editing historical tickets' rails (this fixes the mechanism, not the data); changing the in-session PreToolUse rail hook (this is the CI gate).

CONTEXT FILES: scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs (the union loop + base-ref reading), scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs, packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs (phase-completion evidence model: type ?? gate, p5-complete/p6-acceptance-packet), .adlc/manifest.jsonl (append-only, CI-protected). Memory: [[opencode-native-flush-build-state]] "OPEN SYSTEMIC GAP".

ORIGIN: GitHub issue #137, dogfooded on #104/PR #135. This ticket is self-contained; the issue is background only.

PROBLEM (evidence): Across the opencode T30-T35 arc AND #104, every real correctness/security bug was caught by a cross-model (codex/GPT) adversarial pass ONLY AFTER same-model ADLC P5 prosecution returned a clean SHIP. In #104 same-model P5 passed the security-critical half as airtight, yet codex then found two real bugs (an add-only writer/gate mismatch, and completed-ticket backlog pollution). Root cause: a same-model prosecutor validates the author's own tests, which encode the author's blind spot. ADR-0007 (docs/adr/0007-multimodel-adversarial-review.md) establishes cross-model review but only as RECOMMENDED practice, so it depends on the operator remembering to run it. For trust-root / deny-path / gate-producer changes that is too load-bearing to be optional.

GOAL: For a defined high-risk tier, a clean P5 is IMPOSSIBLE without a recorded cross-model adversarial `approve` from a DISTINCT provider. Convert the recurring lesson from discipline-I-apply into a gate that blocks.

DELIVERABLES:
1. Trust-root-tier classifier. Implement in packages/prosecute (NOT packages/core, which is frozen per CONVENTIONS rule 2; note core/lib/risk-tier.mjs is a DIFFERENT concept — model frontier/direct/ladder tiers). Classify a change (its changed-file set, derivable from a git diff against a base ref, plus the target ticket's scope/rails) as trust-root tier iff it touches any of: scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs, docs/ci/rails-guard.yml, scripts/test/rails-guard-workflow-hashes.json, .adlc/tickets.json, a package that emits an exit-2 gate, a declared rail/deny path, or is a producer of a gated artifact (a tool that writes .adlc/tickets.json or a manifest). Deterministic, offline, unit-testable.
2. Cross-model attestation in the manifest. Define a manifest entry type (e.g. type "cross-model-review") recorded via packages/gate-manifest with data { provider, verdict, baseRef, ticket }. The adversarial-review tool already emits a verdict (exit 0 = approve); wire a record step (a documented `gate-manifest record cross-model-review --data ...` invocation, or a thin helper) so the attestation is machine-checkable. Do NOT trust a provider string the author can freely forge into an approve without having run a review — at minimum bind the entry to the reviewed baseRef/revision so a stale attestation against an old diff does not satisfy a new one (mirror how prosecute already binds revisions).
3. Gate it in prosecute. packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs already reads the manifest (readEntries) and gates P5 on "three distinct dry lenses recorded". Extend it: when the change under prosecution is trust-root tier, P5 additionally requires >=1 cross-model-review approve entry from a provider DISTINCT from the authoring/same-model reviewer, bound to the current revision. Missing -> exit 2 with a clear message naming what is required. Non-trust-root tier: behavior unchanged (no regression).

CLAUDE CODE PLUGIN: plugins/adlc-claude-code — the adlc:prosecutor agent is same-model by default. After a same-model SHIP on a trust-root-tier change it must SURFACE "same-model P5 passed; this tier requires a cross-model pass" and offer the one-command cross-model invocation (it can shell to the local `codex` CLI). Update the P5 text in plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md accordingly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification):
- AC1: The tier classifier returns TRUE for a diff touching each enumerated trust-root/gate/deny/producer surface and FALSE for an ordinary feature diff (e.g. a docs-only or single-app-file change). VERIFY: node --test with positive AND negative fixtures for every surface class.
- AC2: gate-manifest can record and read a cross-model-review attestation carrying provider, verdict, and the reviewed baseRef/revision. VERIFY: node --test round-trips a recorded entry and reads it back; an attestation bound to a stale revision does NOT satisfy the current one.
- AC3: adlc prosecute exits 2 for a trust-root-tier change with no matching cross-model attestation, and exits 0 once a distinct-provider approve bound to the current revision exists; a same-provider (non-distinct) attestation does NOT satisfy the gate. VERIFY: node --test exercising all three branches with fixtures.
- AC4: A NON-trust-root-tier change is unaffected (prosecute outcome identical before/after this ticket). VERIFY: a regression test on an ordinary change.
- AC5: Docs updated — extend docs/adr/0007-multimodel-adversarial-review.md from "recommended" to "gated for the trust-root tier"; update docs/toolkit.md step 6 and the P5 section of plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md. VERIFY: grep the updated language; the phase-router drift test (scripts/test/router-drift.test.mjs) stays green if the skill is generated.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0; `adlc rails-guard` passes for this ticket's diff.

RAILS NOTE: rails intentionally left [] at authoring. Declaring rails now would freeze packages/prosecute/** and packages/gate-manifest/** in CI for ALL PRs until this ticket completes (rails have no start-lifecycle), blocking unrelated work. Declare the real rail set (e.g. freeze the prosecute + gate-manifest test files being made load-bearing) at P3 when the build actually starts.

OUT OF SCOPE: editing packages/core/** (frozen); building the adversarial-review tool itself (external repo voodootikigod/adversarial-review); the risk-tier taxonomy beyond the binary trust-root-tier decision (finer tiers are a follow-up).

tickets.body:
ORIGIN: GitHub issue #138, dogfooded on #104/PR #135. Self-contained; the issue is background only.

PROBLEM (evidence): The MEDIUM bug codex found in #104 was purely a producer/consumer contract mismatch. rails-guard-ci.mjs (the CONSUMER/gate) exempts adding EXACTLY `completed: true` to a base ticket, ADD-ONLY (isCompletionAnnotationOnly rejects a ticket that already has a `completed` field). ticket-prune (the PRODUCER) only skipped `completed === true`, so a rails-less ticket already holding `completed: false`/null was rewritten to `true` — a mutation the gate then DENIES. Net: ticket-prune --write could emit a PR the very gate it exists to satisfy rejects. The two predicates were encoded independently, in different packages, with NO shared test; nothing in the suite exercised the seam. Only cross-model review (reasoning across both files) caught it.

GOAL: Make producer->consumer round-trip coverage a first-class, DETERMINISTIC test pattern so this class of mismatch is caught without a model. Any tool that produces an artifact a gate validates must have a test that runs the tool's ACTUAL output through the gate and asserts acceptance (and that producer-refused cases correspond to gate-denied cases).

DELIVERABLES:
1. ticket-prune round-trip tests (packages/ticket-prune): (a) run `ticket-prune --write` on a fixture repo whose stale ticket is rails-less, then run scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs against the resulting tickets.json diff and assert EXIT 0 (the tombstone output actually merges). (b) A railed-stale fixture: ticket-prune leaves it (needsCeremony) AND a hand-constructed `completed: true` annotation on that railed ticket is DENIED (exit 2) by rails-guard-ci — proving the tool correctly refuses exactly what the gate would reject. (c) The #104 regression: a rails-less ticket already carrying `completed: false` is NOT rewritten by the tool (so no gate-denied mutation is ever produced).
2. ticket-sync round-trip test (packages/ticket-sync): its writes to .adlc/tickets.json (create/push path) produce a diff that rails-guard-ci accepts (exit 0) for the additive case, mirroring the same real-tool-output-through-the-real-gate shape.
3. A documented pattern so future gated-artifact producers follow it: a short note in CONVENTIONS.md (or a skill under plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills) describing the producer->consumer round-trip test requirement, with ticket-prune as the worked example.
4. A drift/coverage check: a test that identifies a NEW .adlc/tickets.json writer lacking round-trip coverage — e.g. scan packages/*/ for a writeJsonAtomic (or equivalent) against a tickets path AND flag the package if it has no test that invokes scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs. Keep it deterministic and offline.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: packages/ticket-prune has a test that runs the real `ticket-prune --write` then the real scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs on the diff, asserting exit 0 for the rails-less tombstone and exit 2 for a hand-made railed-completion. VERIFY: node --test (real subprocesses, in a temp git repo initialized in the test).
- AC2: packages/ticket-sync has an analogous round-trip test for its additive tickets.json write (exit 0). VERIFY: node --test.
- AC3: The round-trip pattern is documented where future authors will see it (CONVENTIONS.md or a skill), naming the #104 mismatch as the motivating example. VERIFY: grep the doc for the pattern; it references ticket-prune + rails-guard.
- AC4: A coverage check flags a tickets.json-writing package that has no rails-guard round-trip test, and passes once ticket-prune + ticket-sync have theirs. VERIFY: node --test — plant a fixture "writer with no round-trip" and assert the check catches it; assert it passes for the real tree.
- AC5: full root `npm test` exits 0; `adlc rails-guard` passes for this ticket's diff.

RAILS NOTE: rails left [] at authoring (same rationale as T39 — avoid freezing packages/ticket-prune/** and packages/ticket-sync/** for all PRs before the build starts). Declare the rail set at P3.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing ticket-prune or rails-guard behavior (the #104 fix already landed on main; this ticket adds the round-trip TESTS + pattern that would have caught it deterministically); editing packages/core/** (frozen).

tickets.body:
ORIGIN: GitHub issue #154, surfaced building T40 (#138) through the T39 cross-model gate. Self-contained; the issue is background.

PROBLEM: `classifyTrustRootTier` in packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs fires the trust-root tier for a change that touches a PRODUCER package (packages/ticket-prune/, packages/ticket-sync/) or an ENFORCEMENT package (packages/rails-guard/, packages/prosecute/, packages/gate-manifest/, packages/build-gate/) via its path-prefix — EVEN when every changed file in that package is a TEST. T40 added only tests to ticket-prune/ticket-sync and was forced through a full multi-round cross-model review, though a test-only diff cannot change the produced artifact and so cannot cause the producer/consumer CONTRACT mismatch the tier exists to gate. (Hollow tests are caught by P5 prosecution/mutation, not by the cross-model contract gate.)

GOAL: A change whose ONLY files in a package-prefix surface are test files does not trigger the tier on the package-prefix basis. Precision fix — reduce over-triggering (which is fail-safe but costly) without weakening any real trust-root detection.

DELIVERABLES:
1. In packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs, add a test-file predicate: a repo-relative POSIX path is a TEST file iff it contains a `/test/` path segment OR its basename matches `*.test.{mjs,js,cjs}`. (Match the repo's actual test conventions — verify against packages/*/test/ and scripts/test/.)
2. For the PACKAGE-PREFIX surfaces ONLY (enforcement-package prefixes + producer prefixes), a changed file counts toward the tier only if it is NOT a test file. If a package prefix matches solely because of test files, that surface does not fire.
3. LEAVE UNCHANGED (still tier regardless of test/non-test): the EXACT trust-root files (scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs, docs/ci/rails-guard.yml, scripts/test/rails-guard-workflow-hashes.json, .adlc/tickets.json), and the RAILS deny-path surface (a changed file matching any ticket's rails glob still tiers — even a test path that IS a declared rail). Note scripts/test/rails-guard-workflow-hashes.json is a test-PATH exact trust-root file: it must STILL tier, so the exact-file check must run before/independent of the test-file exemption.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: a diff touching only `packages/ticket-prune/test/**` (or a `*.test.mjs` in a producer/enforcement package) → `isTrustRootTier: false`, `reasons: []`. VERIFY: unit fixture.
- AC2: the same diff PLUS one non-test file in that package → `isTrustRootTier: true` with the package reason. VERIFY: unit fixture.
- AC3: a change to a trust-root EXACT file (including scripts/test/rails-guard-workflow-hashes.json — a test-path file) still tiers. VERIFY: unit fixtures for each exact file, especially the hash fixture.
- AC4: a change to a file matching a ticket's RAILS glob still tiers, even if that path is a test path. VERIFY: unit fixture with a rails deny-path pointing at a test path.
- AC5: no regression to existing packages/prosecute/test/tier.test.mjs or the CLI/gate tests. VERIFY: full `node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs`.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0 (except the known publish-over-1.3.0 packaging flake); `adlc rails-guard` passes for this ticket's diff.

DOGFOOD NOTE: this ticket edits packages/prosecute (an enforcement package) with LOGIC (non-test) changes, so it is ITSELF trust-root tier and must clear the cross-model gate it refines. Prosecute accordingly (same-model + cross-model).

RAILS NOTE: rails left [] at authoring (rails have no start-lifecycle — see #159; declaring them now would freeze packages/prosecute/** for unrelated PRs). Declare at P3.

OUT OF SCOPE: editing packages/core/** (frozen); changing the cross-model attestation/gate logic (only the tier CLASSIFIER is in scope); the other tier surfaces' semantics beyond the test-file exemption.

tickets.body:
Evaluate and add fleet orchestration on top of the ADLC so parallel development is a first-class, executable capability — not just doctrine. Today the lifecycle runs linearly (one ticket per interactive session) even though the doctrine and data model already contemplate parallelism: ADLC.md describes P4 as "parallel worktrees, single writer per partition", merge-forecast certifies fan-out width from the ticket DAG, and @adlc/core already ships topoSort/computeFloat/scopesOverlap over .adlc/tickets.json edges. What is missing is the orchestrator that dispatches ready tickets to headless workers and walks them through the gates.

=== REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (read first, generalize — do not fork) ===
A working, agy-specific fleet orchestrator exists at ../antigravity-booster (local sibling repo, also on GitHub): the `agb` scheduler (lib/scheduler.mjs ~580 lines, zero-dep, depends on @adlc/core). Its proven mechanics are the design baseline:
- Ticket lifecycle: pending → building (worker in worktree) → gating (build+test) → prosecuting (cross-model refute) → [fixing → gating → prosecuting] → merging (sequential, rebase-first) → merged | failed.
- Event-driven readiness: a ticket dispatches the moment its edge predecessors MERGE (no wave barriers).
- Concurrency via pool semaphores (per-model quota pools in booster; v1 here needs only a single configurable concurrency cap, but the spec must define the pool abstraction so pools can return).
- Deterministic gates in the worktree and again post-merge on main (failed post-merge gate = revert).
- Two-strike regeneration informed by `adlc flail-detector` (a diagnosed flail skips the second strike; a clean one-off failure retries once with dead-ends appended).
- Blocked prosecutions fan out candidate fixes via `adlc consensus-fix` before a single-shot fix round.
- Control flow is code, judgment is models (ADLC D0): the scheduler is deterministic Node; no model decides sequencing.
Also read ADLC.md appendix D2 (fan-out mechanics: predict conflicts, don't resolve them; foundation paths pinned as rails) and the parallel-development conventions in docs/ (worktrees under .worktrees/, sequential merges, no parallel builds).

=== DECISIONS ALREADY MADE (do not relitigate) ===
1. Architecture: a NEW package, packages/fleet (@adlc/fleet), in this repo, following CONVENTIONS.md exactly (zero runtime dependencies, Node 18+ built-ins and @adlc/core via relative import only, bin/fleet.mjs thin CLI, lib/*.mjs pure logic, node:test offline tests, README with exit codes). antigravity-booster later becomes a consumer/sibling of this package; do not modify it in this ticket.
2. Deliverable: the specification AND an MVP implementation, in that order, with the spec gated before any implementation code is written.
3. Worker harness v1: Claude Code headless ONLY (`claude -p`/`--print`, non-interactive, permission mode suitable for unattended worktree builds). The scheduler must talk to workers through a WorkerAdapter seam (dispatch(prompt, {cwd, timeout, env}) → {output, exitCode} plus a charter/AGENTS.md provisioning hook) so codex exec / agy --print / opencode run adapters can be added later WITHOUT touching the scheduler. The adapter interface is a required section of the spec.

=== PHASE 1: SPECIFICATION (gate before code) ===
Write docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md covering at minimum: goals/non-goals; the evaluation (what booster proved, what is agy-specific, what generalizes); plan source and schema; the WorkerAdapter interface; scheduler state machine and persistence/resumability across interruptions; worktree lifecycle (creation under .worktrees/<ticket-id>, branch naming, seeding, cleanup) per the repo's worktree conventions; gate integration (which adlc gates run where: merge-forecast pre-dispatch, rails-guard + ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 inside worker worktrees, build/test gate per ticket, prosecution via the existing prosecute/adversarial-review path, runner evidence expectations); merge policy (sequential, rebase-first, post-merge gate, revert on failure); failure policy (two-strike, flail-detector, consensus-fix); concurrency model (single cap in v1, pool abstraction specified); observability (status file/CLI); threat model (a fleet of unattended writers is a new attack/blast-radius surface — cover rail enforcement in workers, trust-root freeze, and what a compromised/flailing worker can and cannot touch); and out-of-scope items (other harness adapters, quota-pool multiplexing, cross-repo fleets).
HARD REQUIREMENTS the spec must encode:
- Plan source is .adlc/tickets.json itself — the existing contract — NOT a new parallel plan format. The scheduler is a new backlog consumer, so it MUST exclude tickets with completed:true from its active set (repo invariant #104) and MUST respect scope/rails/edges/duration exactly as defined by @adlc/core.
- Tickets whose scopes overlap (core scopesOverlap) are serialized, never dispatched concurrently (merge conflicts are scheduled, not resolved).
- Single writer per partition: at most one worker may hold a given scope at a time; the main checkout is never written by workers.
- Deterministic control flow: no LLM call decides ordering, retries, or merges.
Gate the spec: `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` exits 0, run `adlc premortem` against it and fold findings in, then STOP for explicit user approval (P1 G1) before writing any implementation code. Record the approval in the spec header.

=== PHASE 2: MVP IMPLEMENTATION (packages/fleet) ===
Implement per the approved spec:
1. lib/plan.mjs — load .adlc/tickets.json via @adlc/core, filter completed:true, compute ready set from edges + merged state, enforce scope-overlap serialization.
2. lib/scheduler.mjs — the event-driven loop with a configurable concurrency cap (default small, e.g. 2–3), state machine per the spec, resumable status persisted under .adlc/ (e.g. .adlc/fleet-status.json, in the evidence-ignore set).
3. lib/adapters/claude-code.mjs — the sole v1 WorkerAdapter: spawns `claude -p` with a builder charter (ticket body + scope + rails + dead-ends from prior strikes), cwd = the ticket's worktree, ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and ADLC_TICKET=<id> in env, timeout enforced.
4. lib/worktrees.mjs — create/remove/merge worktrees per repo conventions (may adapt booster's worktrees.mjs logic; keep zero-dep).
5. lib/gates.mjs — run the configured build/test command in the worktree and post-merge; wire flail-detector between strikes.
6. bin/fleet.mjs — `fleet run [--concurrency N] [--dry-run] [--tickets T..,T..]`, `fleet status`; exit codes per CONVENTIONS (0 ok / 1 operational / 2 gate-blocked).
Prosecution wiring may be a stub seam in the MVP if a full cross-model loop is out of reach — but the seam must exist and the spec must say what fills it.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each independently verifiable) ===
- AC1 (spec gated): docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md exists with all required sections above; `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` exits 0; premortem findings are reflected; the file records explicit user approval BEFORE any packages/fleet code was committed. VERIFY: run spec-lint; git log shows the spec commit precedes packages/fleet commits.
- AC2 (conventions): packages/fleet matches CONVENTIONS.md — package.json has zero runtime dependencies (no 'dependencies' beyond nothing; @adlc/core imported by relative path), type module, engines node >=18, bin wired. VERIFY: inspect package.json; grep imports.
- AC3 (scheduler correctness, offline): `npm test` in packages/fleet is green offline with a stubbed WorkerAdapter and stubbed git/gates, covering at minimum: (a) a ticket dispatches only after ALL its edge predecessors merge; (b) completed:true tickets are never dispatched; (c) the concurrency cap is never exceeded; (d) scope-overlapping tickets never run concurrently; (e) two-strike: first failure retries with dead-end context, second failure marks the ticket failed; (f) a diagnosed flail (stubbed flail-detector verdict) skips the second strike; (g) failed post-merge gate triggers revert; (h) status persists and a killed run resumes without re-dispatching merged tickets. VERIFY: run `npm test`; assert each case exists and exercises the real scheduler, not a mock of it.
- AC4 (adapter, offline): the claude-code adapter is tested via an injected exec stub — asserts the spawned argv contains -p/--print and non-interactive flags per the spec, cwd is the worktree, env carries ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and ADLC_TICKET, and timeouts/exit codes map to strike outcomes. No live claude invocation in tests. VERIFY: read the test; run it.
- AC5 (live smoke, manual-ok): a documented end-to-end smoke (README section) runs `fleet run --dry-run` against this repo's real .adlc/tickets.json and prints the computed ready set + dispatch plan without spawning workers or writing worktrees. VERIFY: run it; exit 0; output lists only incomplete tickets with satisfied edges.
- AC6 (no regression): the repo's full test suite still passes and no file outside this ticket's scope changed. VERIFY: `npm test` at root (or the repo's CI command) green; `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` ⊆ scope.
- AC7 (ADR): docs/adr/0010-adlc-fleet-orchestration.md pins the decisions above (new package, tickets.json as plan source, Claude Code-only v1, WorkerAdapter interface, deterministic control flow) with a Threat Model section. VERIFY: file exists; grep for 'WorkerAdapter' and '## Threat Model'.

Suppressions are denied. Out of scope (author follow-on tickets instead of building here): codex/agy/opencode/pi/cursor adapters, per-model quota pools, cross-model prosecution orchestration beyond the seam, GUI/status dashboards, changes to antigravity-booster.
