tickets.body:
Make @adlc/fleet REAL and full-featured: assemble the live-run dependency graph so `fleet run` (non-dry) actually executes end-to-end, and complete the unbuilt parts of the ALREADY-APPROVED spec. This ticket builds on T42 (the MVP: packages/fleet with plan/scheduler/sandbox/protected-paths/lock/worktrees/gates/gate-pipeline/adapter/prosecute/run/bin, 100 offline unit tests, all effects injected). DO NOT re-derive the design or rewrite the MVP — extend it.

=== AUTHORITATIVE CONTRACT (read first) ===
The design is docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md (APPROVED, P1 G1, 6-pass cross-model reviewed) and docs/adr/0010-adlc-fleet-orchestration.md. The MVP already implements the state machine + all policy logic behind an injected-deps seam; what is missing is the LIVE deps assembly and the operator-facing wiring. Read the spec sections cited below as the contract; the MVP's exported functions are the building blocks.

=== WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — DO NOT REBUILD (T42) ===
packages/fleet/lib: plan.mjs (readiness/DAG), scheduler.mjs (advanceTicket state machine, planRound, reconcileResume — all async), sandbox.mjs (resolveSandboxMode, detectBackend, Sandbox, buildSandboxArgv), protected-paths.mjs (scanProtectedPaths), gate-pipeline.mjs (runGatePipeline, collectProtectedCandidates), lock.mjs (acquireLock/isLockLive/forceUnlock), proc.mjs (pidAlive/procStartTimeOf/lockProbes/selfIdentity), worktrees.mjs (createIntegrationBranch/createWorktree/resetWorktree/commitWorker/mergeToIntegration/revertMerge/removeWorktree/abortInProgress/ensureGitignore), gates.mjs (runGates/scopeViolations/checkFlail), env-scrub.mjs (repoCommandEnv/modelPlaneEnv), adapters/claude-code.mjs (provision/dispatch/buildSettings/toPermissionRule), prosecute.mjs (blocking gate over an injected runReview), status.mjs (persist/resume anchors), config.mjs (loadConfig/resolveRunConfig), run.mjs (async runFleet concurrent pool + mergeMutex), mutex.mjs, bin/fleet.mjs (dry-run works; the LIVE path is a documented opError stub). All I/O is injected — this ticket supplies the REAL implementations.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. lib/live-deps.mjs — a `buildLiveDeps({ repo, config, statusDir, runId })` that assembles the real `deps` object runFleet consumes, composing the existing modules with concrete implementations:
   - sandbox: resolveSandboxMode(detectBackend(), operatorOverride) → a Sandbox with a real exec (execFileSync); fail closed (throw an operational error) when refused (spec §7.3).
   - createIntegrationBranch/createWorktree/mergeToIntegration/revertMerge/removeWorktree via worktrees.mjs with defaultGit(repo).
   - provision/dispatch via adapters/claude-code.mjs: dispatch builds the model-plane env (modelPlaneEnv, §7.2 K2) and spawns real `claude -p`; the worker is NOT sandboxed (K2). provision writes the allowlist settings.
   - gate: runGatePipeline wired with the REAL Sandbox, the repo-command env (repoCommandEnv with the sandbox's synthetic HOME), changedPaths from `git diff --name-only <startSha>..HEAD`, templates read from the startSha-committed control files, listProtected from `git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all` filtered to protected prefixes, readBytes reading the worktree copy, and a railsGuard closure invoking `adlc rails-guard --base <startSha> --ticket <id>`.
   - prosecute: a real runReview that spawns `npx adversarial-review --base <startSha> --json` (or the configured provider) over the ticket-local diff, parses findings, and returns { ok:false } (→ fail closed) when no provider is reachable (spec §8.4).
   - postMergeGate: run the configured gate on the integration branch through the sandbox; flail via checkFlail; cleanup via removeWorktree + resetWorktree; openPR via the `gh` CLI when available (§9); statusDir for persistence.
2. lib/preflight.mjs — implement spec §8.0: (a) repo lock acquire (acquireLock + proc.lockProbes/selfIdentity) with stale recovery; (b) clean-tree check (refuse on a dirty main checkout); (c) canary dispatch — a throwaway worktree runs one allowlisted command; if denied/failed, abort operationally BEFORE dispatching real tickets; (d) rail-hook presence probe — warn loudly (never silently) if the ADLC plugin PreToolUse rail hook is not installed for the worker; (e) merge-forecast pre-run (`adlc merge-forecast --json`) recorded into status. Wire preflight into `fleet run` before the loop.
3. Resume wiring — on `fleet run` startup with an existing status for the same recorded run: abortInProgress, prune stale worktrees, reconcileResume(all, status, { isAncestor: (b,r)=>git merge-base --is-ancestor, integrationBranch }); a resumed run must not re-dispatch a merged ticket, and must refuse if the recorded integrationBranch/baseSha is missing/moved (spec §6.4, N2).
4. Evidence + observability — record P4/P5 gate outcomes per ticket via `adlc gate-manifest record` (best-effort; never block the run on a recorder error); ensure .gitignore (ensureGitignore); run the configured `fleet.init` through the sandbox before dispatch (spec §6.3, M1); make `fleet status` show per-ticket state including the prosecution verdict and the last gate output tail.
5. bin/fleet.mjs — replace the live-path opError with the real orchestration: resolve config, run preflight (abort on failure with the right exit code), reconcile resume, then `await runFleet({ all, runId, config: {...resolved, baseSha, sandboxMode}, deps: buildLiveDeps(...) })`; map the summary to exit codes (0 all merged / 2 any failed-or-blocked / 1 operational). Keep --dry-run unchanged. runId is derived from a timestamp (Date is allowed in a normal CLI).
6. scripts/fleet-live-smoke.mjs — a documented END-TO-END smoke: in a disposable scratch git repo it seeds a trivial throwaway ticket (e.g. "create fleet-smoke.txt with the word OK", scope [fleet-smoke.txt], a gate of `test -f fleet-smoke.txt`) and runs a REAL `fleet run` (real sandbox + real claude worker), asserting the ticket reaches merged on the integration branch. It MUST detect missing preconditions (no sandbox backend, no `claude` on PATH) and SKIP with a clear, loud message and exit 0 (so CI is not bricked), running for real only when preconditions are present. It must never mutate the user's real repo — it operates entirely inside a scratch dir it creates and cleans up.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each independently verifiable) ===
- AC1 (live deps assembled + orchestration order): `node --test packages/fleet/test/live-deps.test.mjs` passes — with injected exec/git/spawn stubs it asserts buildLiveDeps produces a deps object whose gate runs build/test THROUGH the sandbox with the scrubbed repo-command env, whose prosecute invokes the review runner over `<startSha>..HEAD`, whose dispatch spawns `claude -p` on the model plane (unsandboxed, provider env retained), and that runFleet driven with these deps advances a ticket build→gate→prosecute→merge in order. VERIFY: run the test.
- AC2 (preflight): `node --test packages/fleet/test/preflight.test.mjs` passes — asserts (i) a failed canary aborts operationally (exit-code path) BEFORE any real dispatch; (ii) a dirty main checkout is refused; (iii) a held live lock refuses while a stale lock is reclaimed; (iv) an absent rail hook emits a loud warning but does not silently proceed; (v) merge-forecast output is recorded into status.
- AC3 (resume end-to-end): `node --test packages/fleet/test/resume.test.mjs` passes — a status with in-flight tickets + a recorded integration branch is reconciled so a branch that is an ancestor of the integration branch is 'merged' (not re-dispatched) and others return to 'pending'; a missing/moved integration branch makes resume refuse; abortInProgress is invoked.
- AC4 (real prosecutor): `node --test packages/fleet/test/live-prosecute.test.mjs` passes — with a stubbed spawn it asserts the review runner invokes adversarial-review with `--base <startSha> --json`, maps a >=medium finding to a blocking verdict (→ ticket routes to fixing), a clean result to pass, and an unreachable provider (spawn error / non-zero without JSON) to a fail-closed 'unavailable' (ticket does not merge).
- AC5 (evidence + status): `node --test packages/fleet/test/evidence.test.mjs` passes — asserts a gate-manifest recorder is invoked per ticket for the P4 and P5 outcomes (stubbed), a recorder error does NOT abort the run, and `fleet status` output includes each ticket's state and prosecution verdict.
- AC6 (live smoke, manual-ok): `node scripts/fleet-live-smoke.mjs` exits 0 — running a REAL end-to-end fleet run on a throwaway ticket in a scratch repo when a sandbox backend AND `claude` are available, and otherwise printing a clear "SKIPPED: <missing precondition>" and exiting 0. VERIFY: run it; it either merges the smoke ticket for real or skips loudly; it never touches the host repo.
- AC7 (no regression): the full packages/fleet suite is green (`node --test packages/fleet/test/*.test.mjs`), `node packages/fleet/bin/fleet.mjs run --dry-run` still exits 0, `adlc rails-guard --base main --ticket T43` exits 0, and `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/core` is empty (packages/core untouched).
- AC8 (P5 prosecuted): the change is prosecuted before merge — `adlc hollow-test --test-cmd "cd packages/fleet && node --test test/*.test.mjs" --base <pre-T43>` shows the new live-wiring tests are load-bearing (survivors limited to I/O-factory/cosmetic lines), and a cross-model adversarial-review of the built code is run and its blocking findings resolved. VERIFY: hollow-test output + review verdict recorded in the PR/commit.

Suppressions are denied. Scope is packages/fleet/** plus scripts/fleet-live-smoke.mjs. Rails: packages/core/** (frozen; delegate all ticket primitives to @adlc/core, never edit core). NOTE the known rails gotcha (github #162): completed T37/T38 froze packages/**·docs/adr/** in the in-session CC hook, so building under packages/fleet needs a user-authorized ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1; packages/core (the real rail) must remain untouched (rails-guard --ticket T43 is the authoritative check). Out of scope (author follow-on tickets): codex/agy/opencode/pi/cursor worker adapters, per-model quota pools, the multi-candidate consensus-fix fix fan-out, additional sandbox backends.

tickets.body:
Flush @adlc/fleet's worker dispatch through ALL native harnesses, not just Claude Code. Today packages/fleet/lib/live-deps.mjs hardcodes `import * as adapter from './adapters/claude-code.mjs'`; the fleet can only dispatch `claude -p` workers. Add a config-driven WorkerAdapter registry plus adapters for codex, antigravity (agy), opencode, pi, and cursor, so `fleet run` can build any harness's ticket in a sandboxed worktree.

=== CONTRACT (read first) ===
The WorkerAdapter interface is defined in docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md §4 and demonstrated by packages/fleet/lib/adapters/claude-code.mjs. An adapter is a pure I/O shim exporting: `name` (string), `pool` (string), `provision({worktree, config, writeJson})` (optional — write a per-worktree settings/permission file; no-op if the harness has none), and `async dispatch({worktree, prompt, timeoutMs, env, exec})` → `{exitCode, output, timedOut}`. NO retry/gate/git logic — that is all scheduler policy (advanceTicket) which every adapter inherits unchanged. The worker runs on the MODEL plane (spec §7.3 K2): it keeps provider egress + its own auth and is NOT wrapped in the no-network sandbox. `exec` defaults to spawnAsync (packages/fleet/lib/spawn-async.mjs) and is injectable for tests.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. packages/fleet/lib/adapters/index.mjs — an adapter REGISTRY: `getAdapter(name)` returns the adapter module (claude-code, codex, agy, opencode, pi, cursor) or throws a clear error for an unknown name; `ADAPTERS` lists the registered names. Fail closed on unknown.
2. packages/fleet/lib/adapters/{codex,agy,opencode,pi,cursor}.mjs — one adapter each, mirroring claude-code.mjs's shape. Each `dispatch` spawns the harness in HEADLESS/non-interactive mode with the ticket prompt and the model-plane env, and maps exit/timeout to the standard result. Ground the DEFAULT invocation per harness but make the command + args OVERRIDABLE via config (config.adapterCommand / config.adapterArgs or a per-adapter config block) so a harness-CLI change is a config fix, not a code change:
   - codex: `codex exec <prompt>` (non-interactive). provision: none (or write the codex approval/config as the sibling codex plugin expects). VERIFY the exact non-interactive flag against the installed codex CLI and note it.
   - agy: `agy --print --model <model> [--sandbox]` with the prompt on stdin (VERIFIED shape: ../antigravity-booster/lib/agy.mjs). model comes from config.model.
   - opencode: `opencode run <prompt>` (headless). VERIFY the run subcommand/flags.
   - pi: headless pi — the child-`pi`-subprocess / `--mode rpc` pattern (docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md notes pi has no -p; the native headless pattern is a child pi subprocess or the SDK createAgentSession/--mode rpc). Implement the best-supported non-interactive form and document the assumption.
   - cursor: `cursor-agent -p <prompt>` (headless print mode). VERIFY the cursor-agent flag.
   Each adapter carries a header comment stating the DEFAULT invocation, its source/confidence, and how to override it.
3. live-deps.mjs — replace the hardcoded claude-code import with `getAdapter(config.adapter ?? 'claude-code')`; thread the selected adapter through provision + dispatch. Default remains 'claude-code' (backward compatible). config.mjs: add `adapter` (default 'claude-code'), plus `model` and the per-adapter command/args override passthrough. An unknown `fleet.adapter` is an operational error surfaced at run start.
4. README + docs/adr note: document the adapter seam, the registered harnesses, the model-plane invariant, and that each default invocation is config-overridable and needs live verification against the installed CLI.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each independently verifiable, OFFLINE) ===
- AC1 (registry): `node --test packages/fleet/test/adapter-registry.test.mjs` passes — getAdapter returns each of the 6 adapters with a name/pool/dispatch, and throws a clear error for an unknown name (fail closed).
- AC2 (per-adapter argv, exec-stub): `node --test packages/fleet/test/adapters-all.test.mjs` passes — for EACH of codex/agy/opencode/pi/cursor, an injected exec stub asserts dispatch spawns the harness's headless command with the ticket prompt, cwd = the worktree, the model-plane env (carries ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT + ADLC_TICKET + retains a provider auth key, unrelated secrets stripped), and that a non-zero/timeout maps to a failed-strike result. No live harness is invoked.
- AC3 (config override): a test asserts an adapter's default command/args are replaced when config supplies an override (so a CLI change is a config fix).
- AC4 (live-deps selection): a test asserts buildLiveDeps({config:{adapter:'codex',...}}) dispatches via the codex adapter (spawns `codex` not `claude`), and that an unknown adapter name fails closed.
- AC5 (backward compatible + no regression): `node --test packages/fleet/test/*.test.mjs` stays green with the default adapter still claude-code; `node packages/fleet/bin/fleet.mjs run --dry-run` exits 0; `adlc rails-guard --base main --ticket T44` exits 0; `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/core` is empty.
- AC6 (P5 prosecuted): hollow-test shows the new adapter tests are load-bearing (survivors limited to I/O-factory/cosmetic), and a cross-model adversarial-review of the built adapters is run and blocking findings resolved. VERIFY: hollow-test output + review verdict in the PR.

Suppressions denied. Scope: packages/fleet/**. Rails: packages/core/**. Out of scope: live end-to-end runs of each harness (documented smoke only); per-model quota pools; harness-specific prosecutor wiring. NOTE the rails gotcha (#162): completed T37 froze packages/**, so building here needs a user-authorized ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1; packages/core (the real rail) must stay untouched.

tickets.body:
## Problem (issue #198)

Shipped tickets are chronically never marked `completed: true` in `.adlc/tickets.json`, so their build-time rails never expire (the T36 rails-completion lifecycle). Stale rails then freeze files against unrelated future work, and `rails-guard-ci` blocks any PR that edits a frozen path. This already blocked PR #196 and required a manual protected-base admin push (PR #199, six raw `completed: true` lines).

The completion half of the lifecycle is missing AND the builder structurally cannot do it: `rails-guard-ci.assertBaseTicketContractsPreserved` denies field changes to existing base tickets in an ordinary PR (`isCompletionAnnotationOnly` exempts ONLY a rails-LESS ticket gaining `completed: true`). Completing a RAILED ticket therefore requires the protected-base admin ceremony — and nothing performs or even surfaces it.

`packages/ticket-prune` already detects shipped tickets (explicit done-status or every declared `scope` glob resolving to a tracked file) and already tombstones the rails-LESS shipped ones in an ordinary PR via a raw add-only `completed: true` edit. It ALSO already classifies the railed shipped ones as `needsCeremony` (blocker `rails-freeze`) instead of completing them — but ONLY inside the `--write` code path, so the dry-run reports `needsCeremony: []` and the drift stays invisible until someone tries to write. There is no command to actually apply the ceremony.

## What to build (extend ticket-prune — direction #1)

1. Surface the drift in dry-run: `ticket-prune` (no `--write`) must compute and report the `needsCeremony` set (active, i.e. `completed !== true`, rail-freezing, shipped tickets) in both the human-readable and `--json` output — the same set the `--write` path computes today. Refactor so the rails-freeze / preexisting-completed-field classification is a pure function shared by the dry-run and write paths.

2. Add a guarded protected-base completion ceremony: a `--ceremony` flag that completes the `needsCeremony` rails-freeze tickets in place using the SAME raw add-only `completed: true` edit ticket-prune already uses for rails-less tombstones (mirrors PR #199 exactly: minimal diff, no manifest entry). It MUST refuse to run and write nothing unless the recorded admin override `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` is set in the environment, because the diff it produces is deliberately one an ordinary PR's rails-guard gate denies — it only lands via the protected-base/admin path. Report completed tickets under a distinct result key (`ceremonyCompleted`). Ceremony handles ONLY the `rails-freeze` blocker; `preexisting-completed-field` tickets stay reported-only (overwriting a deliberately-set field is a different, riskier operation, out of scope).

3. Do NOT weaken the gate: `scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` is a declared rail on this ticket and must not change. The ceremony works WITH the gate (its output lands via the admin path), it does not modify the gate.

4. Wire into `/adlc:adlc-maintain` (all plugin copies) step 3: document that railed-active-shipped tickets surfaced by `ticket-prune` dry-run are drift, and give the exact ceremony command to complete them on the protected base. Update the `ticket-prune` README accordingly.

5. One-time sweep (out of THIS PR): enumerate the current active rail-freezing shipped tickets and document a ready-to-run ceremony command in `docs/specs/ticket-completion-rail-cleanup.md`. The actual sweep lands on `main` via the admin path (like PR #199) and is NOT part of this feature PR — an ordinary PR structurally cannot complete railed base tickets.

## Acceptance criteria (each with a concrete verification method)

- AC1 — dry-run surfaces drift. For a fixture whose shipped railed active ticket exists, `runTicketPrune({ write: false })` returns that ticket in `needsCeremony` with `blocker: 'rails-freeze'`, and both the table and `--json` renderers list it. VERIFY: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/*.test.mjs` (new assertion in run.test.mjs + format.test.mjs). Baseline: today dry-run returns `needsCeremony: []`.

- AC2 — ceremony is admin-gated. With `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS` unset, invoking `--ceremony` writes nothing and exits non-zero with a clear message. VERIFY: run.test.mjs asserts the tickets file is byte-identical and the result is `{ ok: false }` (or bin exits non-zero) when the env is unset.

- AC3 — ceremony completes railed shipped tickets. With `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` and `--ceremony --write`, a shipped railed active fixture ticket gains exactly `completed: true` (no other field changed) and is reported under `ceremonyCompleted`; a still-active (scope not shipped) railed ticket is NOT completed. VERIFY: run.test.mjs asserts the resulting ticket diff is add-only `completed: true` and the active railed ticket is untouched.

- AC4 — rails expire after completion (T36). After the ceremony completes a railed ticket, the rails-guard base-rail union (the `t.completed === true` skip) no longer includes that ticket's rails. VERIFY: a test computes the union before/after and asserts the completed ticket's rails drop out (reusing the union logic / asserting `completed === true`).

- AC5 — existing contract preserved. Rails-less shipped tickets are still tombstoned by the ordinary `--write` path; `preexisting-completed-field` tickets are still reported, never silently rewritten; ceremony does not touch them. VERIFY: existing run.test.mjs cases pass unchanged; a new case asserts `--ceremony` leaves a `preexisting-completed-field` ticket untouched.

- AC6 — gate unchanged. VERIFY: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` is empty (also enforced by the rail on this ticket).

- AC7 — maintenance documents the lifecycle step. `/adlc:adlc-maintain` step 3 (every plugin copy) explains the railed-active-shipped drift signal and the exact ceremony command. VERIFY: `grep` each maintain doc for the ceremony command and the drift explanation.

- AC8 — one-time sweep documented. `docs/specs/ticket-completion-rail-cleanup.md` lists the current railed-active shipped tickets and the exact admin-path command to complete them. VERIFY: read the spec; the listed ids match `ticket-prune --json` `needsCeremony` on `origin/main`.

## Out of scope

- Merge-triggered GitHub Actions automation (issue #198 direction #2).
- A standalone rail-decay gate package (direction #3).
- Directory-store (sharded) ceremony support is secondary — this repo is the legacy flat-file store; if the directory store is not supported by the ceremony, fail closed with a clear message rather than silently mis-handling it.
- Actually landing the one-time sweep on main (that is a separate admin push).

Port Claude Code's `buildgate` PreToolUse enforcing mode into Codex, reusing the EXISTING published `@adlc/build-gate` package rather than extracting new shared logic.

=== CORRECTED UNDERSTANDING (this ticket originally described a fictional 'tool-call budget' mechanism; corrected after reading packages/build-gate directly) ===
`@adlc/build-gate` already exists and is NOT a tool-call budget. It is a context-fitness gate: for a ticket whose risk tier is 'high' (packages/build-gate/lib/risk.mjs computeRiskTier — declared risk:'high', external:true, mutatesIdentity:true, malformed scope/rails, scope/rails touching .adlc/manifest.jsonl or the ticket-store trust root, or category in {contract, architecture}), it denies a PreToolUse call ONLY when the CURRENT SESSION is also 'degraded' (packages/build-gate/lib/depth-signal.mjs isDegraded: tool-call count over a bounded transcript window > 40, OR transcript byte size > 256 KiB). A normal-risk ticket is always allowed; a high-risk ticket in a fresh/shallow session is allowed; only high-risk + degraded denies, and only until the operator either resumes in a fresh session or sets ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 (which is refused unless the override durably records to the gate-manifest via packages/build-gate/lib/override.mjs's recordOverride, itself backed by @adlc/gate-manifest's chain-linked record()).

Claude Code's hook (plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs, computeRiskTierForBuildGate/countToolCallsForBuildGate/denyBuildGate/recordBuildGateBypass) is a VERBATIM INLINE COPY of packages/build-gate/lib/{risk,depth-signal}.mjs's logic, marked 'KEEP IN SYNC with @adlc/build-gate' in comments — because a PreToolUse hook script, invoked from the plugin's INSTALLED location, cannot resolve npm package dependencies at runtime (it only shells out to the globally-installed `adlc` binary for anything requiring @adlc/* code, exactly like plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs's shell classifier is a verbatim inline copy of @adlc/core/lib/shell.mjs for the identical reason). This ticket follows the SAME pattern for Codex: inline-copy, do not re-extract.

CRITICAL DEPENDENCY VERIFIED: Codex's PreToolUse hook payload DOES include a `transcript_path` field (confirmed against the live Codex hooks documentation, code.claude.com-equivalent for Codex — the common hook input fields session_id/transcript_path/cwd/hook_event_name/model/permission_mode are shared across Claude Code and Codex hook payloads), so the depth/bytes context-fitness signal IS computable in Codex exactly as it is in Claude Code. Do not build this without re-confirming that field is present in the actual payload your hook receives, the same way this correction was made by checking the live docs rather than assuming.

=== CONTRACT (write then gate) ===
Author .adlc/specs/codex-build-gate.md before coding (this replaces the prior, factually wrong draft). It must pin: the exact inline-copy boundary (which functions get copied from packages/build-gate/lib/risk.mjs and depth-signal.mjs, with KEEP IN SYNC comments naming the source file/function), the deny output shape (Codex's own convention — plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs's fail(): `console.error(...); process.exit(2)`, NOT Claude Code's structured hookSpecificOutput JSON, since the two harnesses' hook protocols differ), active-ticket resolution (reuse the resolveActiveTicketId() already implemented in plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs rather than re-deriving it a third time), and a drift test comparing the new inline copy's behavior against packages/build-gate's real exports across shared fixtures (packages/core/test/shell.test.mjs is the precedent for this pattern; no equivalent drift test protects Claude Code's own inline copy today, so this ticket does not repeat that gap for Codex).

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. New hook file plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-build-gate.mjs: resolves the active ticket (reusing/sharing resolveActiveTicketId from adlc-rails-guard.mjs), computes risk tier via an inline KEEP-IN-SYNC copy of deriveRiskSignals/computeRiskTier, and if high-risk, reads input.transcript_path, computes the depth/bytes signal via an inline KEEP-IN-SYNC copy of countToolCalls/computeDepthSignal/isDegraded (including the same tailBytes/fileSize windowing Claude Code's hook uses to stay O(MAX_SCAN_BYTES)), and denies (exit 2 + stderr message, Codex's existing convention) when degraded, unless ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 and the override records successfully via a real `adlc gate-manifest record build-gate-bypass` invocation (shelled out, matching the existing gate name Claude Code already uses so manifest entries stay harness-agnostic).
2. hooks.json wiring: add adlc-build-gate.mjs to the existing PreToolUse entry in plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/hooks.json (same matcher regex as adlc-rails-guard.mjs, since both must fire on the same mutating-tool set).
3. Drift test: plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/build-gate.test.mjs importing BOTH the new hook's exported pure functions (risk tier, depth signal, degraded decision) and packages/build-gate's real exports, asserting identical output across shared fixtures — plus coverage for: normal-risk always-allow, high-risk-shallow-allow, high-risk-degraded-deny, missing/unreadable transcript_path fails closed (deny, matching Claude Code's fail-closed behavior for an unverifiable high-risk session), ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS recorded-allow, ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS record-failure still denies.
4. Docs: plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc-rail-build/SKILL.md updated to document the gate and ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS (the REAL env var name, not an invented Codex-specific one).

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

Follow-on to T48. T48 shipped a prose-instructed P5 fan-out for Codex: plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc-prosecute/SKILL.md instructs the operating agent to manually loop through the five lens agents, dedupe, verify, and repeat. plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecutor.mjs re-exports @adlc/core's dedupeFindings/survivesVerification/shouldContinue, but nothing at Codex runtime actually CALLS these functions — they exist for reference-equality testing and documentation only.

plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/prosecute-runner.mjs (T33) is a strictly more rigorous pattern already shipped for OpenCode: runProsecution() is real, unit-tested driver code that actually invokes dedupeFindings/survivesVerification/shouldContinue, fanning out lens/verifier calls through OpenCode's session.create/session.prompt child-session API with a write-disabled tools permission map (wildcard-deny-first allowlist), bounded by maxRounds/maxSessions/maxDry. It is wired to a native `adlc_prosecute`-style tool inside the OpenCode plugin process itself.

Codex's own MCP tool named `adlc_prosecute` (packages/cli/lib/mcp-server.mjs) is NOT equivalent — it only wraps `adlc prosecute --input ... --ticket ...`, i.e. recording already-decided P5 evidence from a file. It has no fan-out/dedupe/verify/loop logic at all. This ticket determines whether Codex's plugin/MCP architecture can support an OpenCode-style deterministic driver, and if so, builds it; if not, it documents why and proposes the best available alternative.

=== CONTRACT (write then gate) ===
Author .adlc/specs/codex-deterministic-prosecution.md as the binding P1 spec before coding. It must answer, with evidence (not assumption): does Codex's plugin architecture (skills, hooks, MCP server, project agents/*.toml) expose ANY mechanism for a running process to spawn an isolated child agent session and receive its reply programmatically — the capability OpenCode's runProsecution() depends on via client.session.create/session.prompt? Sources to check: Codex's own plugin/agent documentation, whether the MCP protocol itself supports server-initiated sampling (MCP's `sampling/createMessage` request type lets an MCP SERVER ask the CLIENT/host to run a model completion — this may be the closest real primitive, if Codex's MCP client implementation supports it). Do not assume feasibility either way — verify against real documentation or a working spike, the same way T52's spec corrected a wrong assumption about Claude Code's hook vocabulary by checking the live docs first.

If a viable mechanism exists: the spec designs a plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecute-runner.mjs mirroring plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/prosecute-runner.mjs's shape (an injectable `ask()` driver, real code calling the @adlc/core helpers, bounded rounds/sessions/dry-streak), wired into the MCP server as a new tool (or an extended `adlc_prosecute` mode) that a Codex session invokes to run the whole loop in one call.

If no viable mechanism exists: the spec documents the finding plainly and proposes the best available fallback — for example, strengthening the existing prose-instructed loop in SKILL.md with stricter machine-checkable self-verification (e.g. requiring the operating agent to paste each round's raw findings JSON into an `adlc prosecute-lint`-style deterministic dedupe/verify checker before proceeding), so at least the dedupe/verify/loop MATH is deterministic even if the individual lens calls remain prose-instructed. This ticket does not ship a broken or aspirational MCP tool either way — the deliverable matches whatever the spec's feasibility finding supports.

=== DELIVERABLES (feasible path) ===
1. plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecute-runner.mjs — a deterministic driver mirroring plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/prosecute-runner.mjs's runProsecution() shape, using the real @adlc/core helpers via plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecutor.mjs.

3. Tests mirroring plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/test coverage for prosecute-runner.mjs (mock `ask()`, bounds, fail-closed unparseable-reply handling).
4. plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc-prosecute/SKILL.md updated to prefer the deterministic tool when available, keeping the T48 prose loop documented as the fallback for hosts/sessions where the tool cannot run.

tickets.body:
A lockstep release rewrites the `version` field in 34 versioned package.json files, the root, package-lock.json, and every host plugin manifest, and repins every @adlc/* dependency range. rails-guard compares changed files BY PATH, so any live rail covering a versioned path failed on EVERY release — regardless of whether the ticket owning that rail had anything to do with the release.

This blocked three consecutive changes (#218/#219, and #226 twice). Each was cleared by completing stale tickets (#221, #227). That was the correct remedy for the DRIFT — those tickets genuinely had shipped — but it is not a remedy for the COLLISION, and treating it as one obscured the real defect.

Staleness was never the cause. A ticket correctly in flight with rails: ["packages/build-gate/**"] blocks every release for its entire lifetime, and completing it to unblock one would be a lie. The only other exit was bypassing the guard on releases, which establishes "releases route around rails-guard" as normal practice — the exact norm a freeze gate exists to prevent.

=== DECISION ===

A manifest change whose ONLY differences are version fields and lockstep @adlc/* dependency repins is not a rail edit. A rail exists to stop an agent editing frozen BEHAVIOUR mid-build; a version bump changes none. Recorded as docs/adr/0012-version-only-rail-exemption.md.

Scope, deliberately narrow:
- eligible files: basename package.json, plugin.json, marketplace.json. NOT package-lock.json.
- eligible paths: version, metadata.version, plugins[i].version, <depField>["@adlc/*"].
- eligible values: both sides plain strings — exact semver for versions, ^/~/exact for ranges.
- everything else is an ordinary rail violation.

OFF unless a content resolver is supplied, so callers that cannot read real file content keep the original stricter behaviour. A resolver that throws or returns null denies.

scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs required NO change: it delegates the rail-glob diff to packages/rails-guard/bin, so fixing the canonical package fixed the CI gate. That matters because the CI script is an immutable trust root whose edit would need the protected-base admin ceremony.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

AC1. A release bump on a tree with a LIVE ticket railing packages/<x>/** passes rails-guard.
AC2. A real behaviour edit to a file under that same live rail still FAILS — proven by a test, since a fix that merely weakened the guard would also satisfy AC1.
AC3. A version bump that smuggles any non-version manifest change (added dependency, scripts block, changed main, reordered exports keys, array-to-object swap) still FAILS.
AC4. The exemption denies on: unparseable JSON either side, a missing side (file added or deleted), a non-object document, any container whose key set or kind changed, any differing path outside the eligible set, any eligible path whose value is not a plain string of the expected shape.
AC5. No immutable trust root is eligible for the exemption, asserted by test so it stays true if the trust-root list grows.
AC6. The exemption cannot be enabled by accident: omitting the content resolver preserves the original behaviour.
AC7. Mutation calibration — each of the load-bearing mechanisms, when deleted, fails at least one test. Specifically the container-shape record, the declaration-order key capture, the container-kind marker, and the symlink/mode guard.

=== PROSECUTION RECORD ===

The first implementation was prosecuted (P5) and FOUR confirmed defects were found, two reproduced as working rail bypasses through the real binary:

1. Object keys were sorted before comparison. Node resolves conditional `exports` first-match-wins, so reordering {"node":...,"default":...} flips which module a frozen package loads while every leaf value stays identical. Keys are now recorded in declaration order.
2. Container kind was not recorded, so [{...}] and {"0":{...}} recorded identically and an array could be swapped for an object undetected. The kind is now part of the record.
3. The resolver used readFileSync, which follows symlinks, while git show returns the blob. A railed manifest replaced by a symlink to identical text compared equal and was exempted, with the link target then living outside the rail. Now requires a regular file at HEAD, a regular blob at base, and an unchanged executable bit.
4. The predicate call sat outside its try, so a pathologically nested manifest threw out of the unbounded walk uncaught, converting a gate decision (exit 2) into an operational crash (exit 1). Moved inside the try; the walk gained a depth cap that denies rather than throws.

The most instructive finding was a HOLLOW TEST, not a bypass: deleting the single line recording container shape — the mechanism the whole design rests on — failed ZERO of 110 tests. Every structural test passed incidentally through leaf differences and never exercised that path; empty containers ("scripts": {}) change no leaf at all. AC7 exists because of this.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===

Option 3 of #228 (reject metadata-covering rail globs at ticket-authoring time) is tracked as #235. It requires moving glob matching into @adlc/tickets, because @adlc/core already depends on @adlc/tickets and so tickets cannot import globMatch from core without a cycle. That is a public-surface refactor, and it is complementary hygiene rather than a fix.

=== TIER ===

This change modifies packages/rails-guard, an ENFORCEMENT package. Per ADR-0007 a same-model P5 pass is not sufficient: a cross-model adversarial approve from a provider distinct from the author is required before merge.

PR: #234. Issue: #228. Ticket authored after implementation to carry the cross-model attestation; the prosecution record above is the contemporaneous evidence.

=== RAILS CORRECTION ===

This ticket originally railed its own two test files. That was a mis-authoring, and the guard caught it: the tests were still being written — cross-model prosecution rejected the first fix and demanded new cases — so freezing them blocked the very work the ticket describes. A rail is for freezing what the builder must NOT change; it is not for the artifacts the ticket is actively producing.

Rails removed under authorization rather than bypassed. Two things are worth recording:

1. The PreToolUse rail hook intercepts Edit/Write tool calls but NOT shell writes. Appends made with cat >> and perl -pi to these frozen files went through unblocked. That is the exact gap scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs exists to backstop at commit time, and it is why that backstop is not redundant. Filed separately.

2. The correct rail for a ticket like this would freeze the paths the change must NOT touch (for example the trust roots, or a sibling package), not the files it creates.
tickets.title: A version-only manifest edit must not read as a rail edit (#228)

Build the foundation of @adlc/ticket-sync per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-27-external-ticketing-sync-design.md (sections 'Schema bedrock', 'Hard constraints', field-definition table). Create packages/ticket-sync as a zero-runtime-dependency package (CONVENTIONS rule 1; Node 18+ built-ins only) WITHOUT editing packages/core (CONVENTIONS rule 2 — core is frozen). Deliver: lib/schema.mjs (single declarative field definition = source of truth), lib/validate.mjs (definition-driven validator over the rich schema), lib/canonical.mjs (canonical JSON: sorted keys, LF, stable number formatting, CRLF-insensitive equality), scripts/gen-schema.mjs (emits schemas/adlc-ticket.schema.json, adlc-block.schema.json, adlc-config.schema.json, adlc-sync-state.schema.json from the definition), and the committed schema files.

Acceptance criteria (each verifiable):
1. `npm test` green for packages/ticket-sync/test/{schema,validate,canonical}.test.mjs.
2. Drift gate: test regenerates schemas in-memory and asserts byte-equality with the committed schemas/*.json; editing the definition without regenerating fails the test (verify by mutating the definition in a scratch run).
3. Cross-validator agreement: a corpus of tickets core's validateTicket accepts is also accepted by the rich validator on shared fields (asymmetric subset direction).
4. No file under packages/core is modified (verify: `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/core` is empty).
5. Package declares zero runtime dependencies (verify: no 'dependencies' beyond @adlc/* in package.json).

tickets.body:
Implement lib/block.mjs in @adlc/ticket-sync per the spec sections 'The block' and 'Validity Gate' (block cases). The block is JSON (JSON.parse — no YAML, zero-dep) wrapped in reserved HTML-comment sentinels `<!-- adlc:begin v=1 key=<uuid> -->` ... `<!-- adlc:end -->`. parseBlock(body) returns {prefix, block, suffix, version, key, formatErrors}; serializeBlock(prose{prefix,suffix}, fields) reproduces the body. Field validation delegates to T1's validator (no second schema). Depends on T1.

Acceptance criteria:
1. packages/ticket-sync/test/block.test.mjs green covering: lossless round-trip (prefix AND suffix prose preserved verbatim); missing/duplicate/unbalanced sentinels -> fail closed with an error naming the offending line; garbled JSON -> fail closed; present-but-invalid block (e.g. malformed rails) -> fail closed (NEVER degrade to 'no rails'); `$schema` key excluded from canonical equality; sentinel `v` greater than supported max -> fail closed.
2. A human-authored ```json fence in prose outside the sentinels is ignored.
3. Body model {prefix, block, suffix} is preserved across a parse->serialize cycle.

Implement `adlc ticket pull` (dry-run by default; --write applies) per the spec data-flow 'Pull', 'Sidecar', 'Validity Gate', 'Sync vs the rails trust root', and 'Lock + atomic write'. Deliver: lib/gh.mjs (execFile wrapper — argv only, no shell, C4), lib/providers/github.mjs (read/map), lib/provider.mjs (interface, no registry), lib/reconcile.mjs (pure 3-way base/local/remote; base from sidecar syncedHash; missing/corrupt base fails safe to CONFLICT), lib/config.mjs (+ adlc-config validation, repo auto-detect, issue selector), lib/store.mjs (writeTicketsAtomic + mkdir lock sharing .adlc/tickets.lock; sidecar .adlc/ticket-sync.state.json gitignored rebuildable cache), lib/rails-guard-sync.mjs (rails superset / scope subset guard + forensic record), and register the `ticket` tool in packages/cli/lib/registry.mjs. Single repo-qualified id space gh:owner/repo#n, owner/repo lowercased to match loadTickets equality; unresolved edges FAIL CLOSED (no silent drop); pagination explicit (truncation -> exit 1, never deletion). Depends on T2.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/{reconcile,github,config,store,validity,rails-guard-sync}.test.mjs green; all offline via an injected gh runner with canned --json fixtures.
2. reconcile: remote-only/local-only/both-changed(conflict)/both-equal(converged); local-only ticket survives pull; out-of-selection survives.
3. Validity Gate: id normalization unifies T<n>/gh: spellings; an unresolved edges[].to fails closed (exit 2), not dropped; resolution-checked set == bytes written.
4. rails-guard-sync: rails non-superset and scope-widen refused without --allow-rail-narrowing; forensic record written.
5. pull is dry-run without --write (verify no file mutation); exit codes 0/1/2 per matrix.

tickets.body:
Implement `adlc ticket push` and `adlc ticket sync` (dry-run by default; --write applies) per the spec data-flow 'Push'. Deliver: lib/outcomes.mjs (reduce .adlc/manifest.jsonl -> per-ticket status: latest-per-gate, verdict=latest P5 entry, no P5 -> no pass label), lib/status-render.mjs (labels mutually-exclusive within statusLabels + a canonical timestamp-free status comment; both display-only, never authoritative), and github write ops (updateIssueBody, ensureLabels, upsertStatusComment, createIssue). Create is idempotent: stable sentinel key, adopt off the already-paginated pull list (not the eventually-consistent search index), persist {nodeId,number} into pendingCreates before id-reassignment, >1 key match fails closed; on create reassign id T<n>->gh:owner/repo#n, rewrite every edges[].to store-wide, migrate manifest evidence to the new id. Transfer/renumber reuses the same reassign+edge-rewrite path. Depends on T3.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/outcomes.test.mjs green: multiple verdicts (latest wins), none (no fabricated pass), per-gate latest.
2. test/github.test.mjs idempotency: push twice against a recording fake -> second run makes no mutating calls; create adoption finds an existing keyed issue; a simulated lost local write does NOT duplicate; id reassignment rewrites edge references.
3. push is dry-run without --write; partial failure -> per-issue result list, exit 1.
